---
title: End-to-End TypeGen Pipeline
description: Architecture of the Python-to-TypeScript schema and route generation pipeline across OpenAPI, Routes, Inertia PageProps, and AsyncAPI Channels.
---

# End-to-End TypeGen Pipeline

When `ViteConfig(types=True)` (or `TypeGenConfig(...)`) is enabled, Litestar Vite turns Python route handlers, DTOs, `msgspec.Struct` / Pydantic models, Inertia page components, and WebSocket / Channels streams into compile-time checked TypeScript artifacts without manual synchronization.

[Interactive Architecture Diagram: diagram-typegen-pipeline.html]
---

## Four-Stage Generation Lifecycle

### Python Introspection

On application startup (or when running `litestar assets generate-types`), Litestar Vite inspects the initialized `Litestar` instance:

- **OpenAPI Schema (`codegen/_openapi.py`)**: Confines all Litestar OpenAPI access (`OpenAPISupport`, `SchemaCreator`, `build_schema_name_map`) to a single private seam, serializing a deterministic OpenAPI 3.1 document with sorted keys.
- **Route Metadata (`codegen/_routes.py`)**: Extracts HTTP and WebSocket routes (`extract_route_metadata`), typed path and query parameters, `operationId` links, and Inertia `component` annotations while excluding internal proxy/HMR endpoints.
- **Inertia Page Metadata (`codegen/_inertia.py`)**: Maps every route with `component="..."` to its return-type schema reference or inline TypeScript type, plus registered `InertiaConfig` shared props.
- **AsyncAPI 3.0 Channels (`generate_asyncapi_schema`)**: When `litestar-asyncapi` (`AsyncAPIPlugin`) or `ChannelsPlugin` is registered, exports WebSocket and pub/sub channel payloads to `asyncapi.json` (and unlinks stale `asyncapi.json` / `channels.ts` files if the plugin is removed).

### Deterministic Disk Writes

Every exported JSON and TypeScript file is written through a content-hash check (`write_if_changed` in both Python and TypeScript). If the serialized byte content is identical to the file already on disk, the file's `mtime` is preserved so Vite's watcher never triggers redundant HMR rebuild loops.

### Vite TypeGen Plugin

On the JavaScript side, `createLitestarTypeGenPlugin` (shared across `litestar-vite-plugin`, `/astro`, `/sveltekit`, and `/nuxt`) watches the exported JSON files with a 300ms debounce window and runs four emitters:

| Input Artifact | Emitter | Generated Output | Primary Symbols |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `openapi.json` | `@hey-api/openapi-ts` | `api/types.gen.ts`, `api/sdk.gen.ts` | Typed REST client, request/response models, optional Zod schemas |
| `routes.json` | `generate_routes_ts` / `routes.ts` | `routes.ts` | `route()`, `toRoute()`, `wsRoute()`, `routeDefinitions`, `RouteName` |
| `routes.json` + `openapi.json` | `emit-schemas-types.ts` | `schemas.ts` | `FormInput<R>`, `FormResponse<R, Status>`, `SuccessResponse<R>` |
| `inertia-pages.json` | `emit-page-props-types.ts` | `page-props.ts` | `PageProps`, `PagePropsFor<C>`, `InertiaPageProps<C>` |
| `asyncapi.json` | `emit-channels-types.ts` | `channels.ts` | `ChannelMap`, `ChannelName`, `ChannelPayload`, `bindTypedChannels()` |
| `.litestar.json` (`staticProps`) | `emit-static-props-types.ts` | `static-props.d.ts` | `declare module "virtual:litestar-static-props"` |

### HMR Notification

Whenever any generated TypeScript file changes on disk, `createLitestarTypeGenPlugin` dispatches a custom Vite WebSocket event (`litestar:types-updated`) and logs the regeneration duration in milliseconds.

---
title: Dev Proxy & .litestar.json Bridge
description: How Litestar and Vite 7+ coordinate via .litestar.json, the hot file, and the single-port AnyIO HTTP/WebSocket proxy.
---

# Dev Proxy & Runtime Bridge

Running two separate servers during development (`localhost:8000` for Python and `localhost:5173` for Vite) traditionally introduces CORS configuration drift, split cookie origins, and broken WebSocket HMR paths behind reverse proxies. Litestar Vite eliminates two-port friction with a **single-port AnyIO streaming proxy** and a deterministic **`.litestar.json` configuration bridge**.

[Interactive Architecture Diagram: diagram-dev-proxy.html]
---

## The Runtime Bridge Handshake

Python (`ViteConfig`) is the single source of truth for asset paths, ports, executors, and type-generation flags.

1. **Python Startup (`VitePlugin.on_app_init`)**: Before launching or connecting to Vite, `VitePlugin` serializes resolved paths (`bundleDir`, `resourceDir`, `staticDir`, `assetUrl`, `hotFile`, `manifest`), runtime settings (`mode`, `proxyMode`, `host`, `port`, `executor`, `litestarPort`), typegen settings (`types`), and static props (`staticProps`) into `.litestar.json`.
2. **Vite Startup (`readBridgeConfig`)**: In `vite.config.ts`, `litestar({ input: ["src/main.ts"] })` reads `.litestar.json` via `readBridgeConfig()`. You never have to repeat `bundleDir`, `assetUrl`, or `types.output` in TypeScript.
3. **Ephemeral Port Discovery (`hot` file)**: Once Vite's HTTP server binds to its port, `litestar-vite-plugin` writes the active dev server URL (for example `http://127.0.0.1:5173`) to `${bundleDir}/${hotFile}` (`public/hot` by default) and removes the file automatically on process exit (`SIGINT`, `SIGTERM`, `SIGHUP`).

---

## Single-Port AnyIO Streaming Proxy

When `runtime.dev_mode=True` and `proxy_mode="vite"` (the default), browser clients connect **exclusively** to the Litestar port (`http://127.0.0.1:8000`):

- **Zero Runtime HTTPX Dependency**: `ViteProxyMiddleware` uses raw `anyio.connect_tcp` sockets for HTTP/1.1 request/response streaming and `wsproto` for WebSocket frame tunneling (`vite-hmr`), keeping the core package lightweight.
- **Dynamic Target Resolution**: On each proxied request, `ViteProxyMiddleware` reads the target host and port from the `hot` file (caching by mtime), so if Vite restarts on a new port, Litestar routes to the new port without restarting Python.
- **HMR WebSocket Tunneling (`/static/vite-hmr`)**: `litestar-vite-plugin` configures Vite's HMR channel (`server.ws` on Vite 8.1+ / `server.hmr` on Vite 7) with `path: "vite-hmr"`, which Vite prefixes with `assetUrl` (`/static/vite-hmr`). `ViteProxyMiddleware` intercepts WebSocket upgrades on that path and tunnels frames bidirectionally between the browser and Vite.
- **HTML Transformation (`/__litestar__/transform-index`)**: In SPA mode, `AppHandler` delegates dev-time HTML entry transformation to Vite's internal middleware pipeline (`server.transformIndexHtml`) and injects `window.__LITESTAR_CSRF__` before returning the HTML shell.

---

## Production Static Serving & Granian Native Placement

When `dev_mode=False`, `ViteProxyMiddleware` is not mounted. Instead, `VitePlugin` registers static file serving for `bundle_dir` and `static_dir` with two Router-level hooks:

| Hook Class | Responsibility | Why Attached at Router Level |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `_StaticBeforeRequestHook` | Returns 404 Not Found for build metadata files (`manifest.json`, `.vite/manifest.json`, `ssr-manifest.json`, `hot`). | Keeps `StaticFilesConfig.has_asgi_overrides()` equal to `False` so `litestar-granian` can serve static files directly inside Rust (`StaticPlacement.NATIVE`). |
| `_StaticAfterRequestHook` | Sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` on hashed bundle paths (`/static/assets/*`). | Picklable slotted callable class (`__slots__`) that survives `copy.deepcopy(router)` during Litestar route registration. |

---

---
title: Architecture Overview
description: Visual overview of how Litestar (Python ASGI) and Vite 7+ coordinate across operating modes, development HMR proxying, and production asset serving.
---

# Architecture Overview

Litestar Vite bridges two runtimes with distinct responsibilities:

- **Litestar (Python ASGI)** owns routing, dependency injection, authentication guards, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI schema metadata, CSRF protection, and HTML shell or JSON serialization.
- **Vite 7+ (JavaScript / TypeScript)** owns ES module transformation, Hot Module Replacement (HMR), CSS/Tailwind pipelines, SSR module execution (`RunnableDevEnvironment`), and production Rollup/Rolldown bundling.

Use the interactive switcher below to inspect how HTML shell ownership, routing, and data transport change across the four operating modes:

[Interactive Architecture Diagram: diagram-operating-modes.html]
---

## Operating Mode Matrix

| Operating Mode | HTML Shell Owner | Router Owner | Primary Data Transport | Typical Stack |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `mode="spa"` | `AppHandler` (`index.html`) | Client router | `@hey-api/openapi-ts` + `route()` | React Router, Vue Router, TanStack Router |
| `mode="hybrid"` | `AppHandler` / Jinja + SSR | Litestar (`component=`) | Inertia.js `PageProps` JSON | `@inertiajs/react`, `@inertiajs/vue3`, `@inertiajs/svelte` |
| `mode="template"` | Jinja2 (`vite()`, `vite_hmr()`) | Litestar controllers | Server HTML + `<litestar-island>` + HTMX | Jinja2, HTMX (`hx-swap="json"`), WebSocket/SSE |
| `mode="framework"` | Meta-framework server | Meta-framework router | `/api/*` proxy + shared TypeGen | Astro 5, SvelteKit, Nuxt 4 |

---

## Development vs. Production Execution

During development (`dev_mode=True`), Litestar proxies asset and HMR WebSocket traffic to a live Vite 7+ process over a single browser origin (`127.0.0.1:8000`). In production (`dev_mode=False`), Node is not required for static assets: `ViteAssetLoader` resolves hashed bundles from `manifest.json` while Litestar serves immutable static files directly.

[Interactive Architecture Diagram: diagram-dev-vs-prod.html]
---

---
title: SSR, Server Fragments, & IPC
description: Internal architecture of Inertia.js lifecycle, Dev TCP vs. Prod Stdio SSR IPC transports, SSRCircuitBreaker, and <litestar-island> hydration.
---

# SSR, Server Fragments, & IPC

Litestar Vite provides a unified inter-process communication (IPC) engine (`BaseIPCTransport`) shared by both **Inertia.js Server-Side Rendering (`InertiaResponse`)** and **Standalone Server Fragments (`FragmentEngine` / `vite_fragment`)**.

[Interactive Architecture Diagram: diagram-ssr-ipc.html]
---

## Development vs. Production IPC Transports

| Transport | Active When | Wire Protocol | Process & Cache Model |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TCPStreamIPCTransport` | `dev_mode=True` | HTTP/1.1 `POST /__litestar_ssr__` over pooled `httpx2` | Executes SSR modules inside Vite 7+'s `RunnableDevEnvironment` (`ServerModuleRunner`). Rejects browser requests (`Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site` headers return 403). Recursively invalidates parent importer chains on HMR updates. |
| `StdioIPCTransport` | `dev_mode=False` (`ssr_transport="stdio"` or `"auto"`) | Newline-delimited JSON (`IPCRequest` / `IPCResponse`) over `stdin` / `stdout` pipes | Spawns a persistent worker (`startSsrWorker` from `litestar-vite-plugin/ssr-worker` using streaming `TextDecoder` with zero `node:readline` imports, compatible with Node, Bun, and Deno). Drains `stderr` concurrently into a bounded 100-line ring buffer to prevent 4 KB OS pipe buffer deadlocks. Exits with status `0` on `stdin` EOF once in-flight renders drain, and restarts on crash up to `max_restarts`. |
| `WasmIPCTransport` | `dev_mode=False` (`ssr_transport="wasm"` or auto-detected via `resolve_ssr_transport`) | In-process JSON dispatch via `globalThis.__litestar_ssr_dispatch__` | Evaluates the self-contained ES-module `ssr.js` bundle (`ssr.noExternal: true`) inside an embedded QuickJS context (`litestar-vite[wasm]`) on a dedicated worker thread via `Context.module`. Enforces per-request `set_time_limit(timeout)` and rebuilds the context automatically after a timeout. |

---

## Circuit Breaker & Client Fallback

Every SSR and fragment render passes through `SSRCircuitBreaker`:

1. **`CLOSED` (Normal Operation)**: Requests are dispatched to the active `BaseIPCTransport`.
2. **`OPEN` (Tripped after `failure_threshold` consecutive errors)**: Subsequent requests bypass IPC immediately for `recovery_timeout` seconds. When `fallback_to_client=True`, `InertiaResponse` returns the client-side HTML shell with `data-page` (or `<script type="application/json" id="app_page">`) so users never see a 500 page when an SSR component throws.
3. **`HALF_OPEN` (Probe Window)**: After `recovery_timeout` elapses, a single probe render is dispatched. A successful render resets the breaker to `CLOSED`; a failure re-opens the circuit.

---

## HTML Splicing & Island Hydration

Once the JavaScript runtime returns `{ head: string[], body: string }` (for Inertia SSR) or `{ html: string, head: string[], css: string[] }` (for `FragmentEngine`):

- **Right-to-Left Offset Splicing (`inject_inertia_ssr_tags`)**: An `HTMLParser` state machine (`_InertiaSlots`) locates `<!--inertia-head-->` / `@inertiaHead` inside `<head>` and `<!--inertia-->` / `@inertia` inside `<body>` (ignoring matches inside `<script>`, `<style>`, `<pre>`, or `<code>`) and splices the rendered markup from right to left by character offset.
- **Progressive Island Hydration (`<litestar-island>`)**: When a fragment is rendered with `mode="island"`, `renderFragment()` wraps the server HTML in `<litestar-island data-island-id="..." data-island-component="..." data-island-props="...">` and appends a module loader for `clientEntry`. On the client, `hydrateIslands()` (`litestar-vite-plugin/fragments/client`) serializes mount/teardown transitions with a revision counter and restores the original SSR markup on disconnect so HTMX swaps never leave orphaned roots.

---

## Inertia.js Request & Prop Evaluation Lifecycle

In `mode="hybrid"`, `InertiaPlugin` and `InertiaResponse` implement the complete Inertia.js wire protocol across initial HTML visits, `X-Inertia` JSON transitions, deferred prop groups, partial reloads, and 303/409 status codes:

[Interactive Architecture Diagram: diagram-inertia-lifecycle.html]

---

<!-- Source: docs/changelog.md -->

# Changelog

Notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## 0.33.0 - 2026-11-03

- Added first-class Deno 2.x and Bun runtime support: `RuntimeConfig.executor` is detected from
  `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`, `deno.lock`/`deno.json`/`deno.jsonc`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`,
  `yarn.lock`, `package-lock.json`, or `package.json#packageManager`; `DenoExecutor` uses
  `deno task`/`deno install`/`deno outdated --update`; type generation emits Deno/Bun-compatible
  module specifiers; `litestar assets doctor` warns on executor/lockfile mismatches. New optional
  extras `litestar-vite[node]`, `[bun]`, and `[deno]` install PEP 425 runtime wheels and
  `RuntimeConfig.provisioning_mode` (`auto`/`wheel`/`nodeenv`/`system`) controls where
  binaries are resolved from. ([#390](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/390))
- Added Vite backend-integration and ASGI modernization: recursive `<link rel="modulepreload">` and
  transitive CSS injection from the manifest graph, CSP `nonce` and SRI `integrity` propagation,
  RFC 8288 `Link` preload headers (`RuntimeConfig.link_preload_headers`), opt-in `103 Early Hints`
  via the ASGI `http.response.early_hint` extension (`RuntimeConfig.early_hints`), immutable
  `Cache-Control` for hashed files under the Vite `assets` directory
  (`RuntimeConfig.immutable_cache_headers`), `404` for `manifest.json`/`.vite/manifest.json`/
  `ssr-manifest.json`/`.litestar.json`/`hot` on the static route, and binary WebSocket frame
  forwarding in the HMR proxy. Static hooks are router-level and keep Granian
  `StaticPlacement.NATIVE` eligibility; they do not apply to Granian-native file hits. ([#390](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/390))
- Added self-contained production SSR: the npm plugin now defaults `ssr.noExternal: true` for
  production SSR builds and `litestar-vite-plugin/ssr-worker` no longer imports `node:readline`,
  so the same `ssr.js` runs under Node, Bun, Deno, and QuickJS. The worker exits on
  `stdin` EOF after draining in-flight requests. **Breaking:** projects that relied on SSR bundles
  resolving packages from `node_modules` at runtime must opt out with `ssr: { noExternal: [] }`
  (or a package allow-list) in `vite.config.ts`; see [Migrating to v0.33](learn/migration-0-33.md). ([#390](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/390))
- Added experimental in-process `WasmIPCTransport` (`litestar-vite[wasm]`, QuickJS) with ES-module
  bundle loading, a global shim (`TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`, `queueMicrotask`, `setTimeout`),
  per-request engine time limits, and automatic context rebuild after a timeout.
  `RuntimeConfig.ssr_transport` (`auto`/`stdio`/`wasm`) and `resolve_ssr_transport` select the
  production transport. ([#390](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/390))
- Added WebSocket route metadata extraction (`WebSocketRoute` with `protocol="websocket"` and
  AsyncAPI `channel_key` alignment) and type-safe `wsRoute()` / `route.ws()` helpers in generated
  `routes.ts` and `litestar-vite-plugin/helpers`. ([#390](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/390))
- Redesigned the documentation with modular framework and Inertia.js guides, interactive SVG architecture diagrams, runnable standalone examples, and automated Python/TypeScript/CLI reference generation. ([#390](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/390))
- Fixed `process_session_props()` and `process_shared_prop_types()` in `litestar_vite.codegen` emitting raw Python built-in type names (`str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `dict`, `list`) into `page-props.ts` instead of mapping them through `python_type_to_typescript()`. ([#389](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/issues/389))
- Updated `_configure_static_files()` documentation and static router handler tests to reflect handler-level `opt` scoping without stale `litestar-security` parent-layer exclusion comments. ([#356](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/issues/356))

## 0.32.0 - 2026-09-28

- Added AsyncAPI export and TypeScript channel type generation from a registered
  `litestar-asyncapi.AsyncAPIPlugin`. Applications without that plugin no longer receive
  inferred realtime schemas. ([#368](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/368))
- Added IPC subsystem (`litestar_vite.ipc`) using `StdioIPCTransport` for production `stdio` workers and `TCPStreamIPCTransport` for development Vite `ModuleRunner` SSR, with circuit breaking (`SSRCircuitBreaker`) and client-side hydration fallback. ([#369](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/369))
- Replaced `httpx` with `httpx2` as the runtime HTTP client for pooled asset and framework HTTP proxying;
  development SSR RPC also uses a managed `httpx2` pool inside `TCPStreamIPCTransport`,
  while production SSR keeps the stdio IPC protocol. ([#369](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/369))
- Declared `markupsafe` as a runtime dependency so a minimal installation can import the
  asset loader without installing the optional Jinja template engine.
- Added Vite `ModuleRunner` dev SSR plugin (`RunnableDevEnvironment.runner`) and recursive importer cache
  invalidation for in-memory SSR during development. ([#369](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/369))
- Restricted development SSR to configured entrypoints and component roots, rejecting
  browser-origin RPC requests and paths outside those roots.
- Added server-side UI component fragment rendering (`ComponentResponse`, Jinja `vite_fragment`
  global, and `<litestar-island>` custom element) with scoped CSS chunk injection from `manifest.json`
  for HTMX partial swaps and Jinja templates. ([#369](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/369))
- Updated Inertia HTML transform to use slot/token replacement (`<!--inertia-head-->` and
  `<!--inertia-body-->`) with fallback to `#app` selector replacement, and routed SSR requests
  through the IPC transport layer. ([#369](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/369))
- Enforced Vite 7+ minimum runtime baseline (`>=7.0.0`), updated scaffolding templates for Vite 8 and
  `rolldownOptions`, and bundled dev SSR, worker, and fragment entrypoints in the JS package. ([#369](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/369))
- Fixed SSR token replacement preserving user data, strict failure behavior when the circuit
  breaker is open, and Jinja fragment rendering with dependency injection and response caching.
  Bounded worker startup/write deadlines and cancellation-safe cleanup prevent stranded
  requests and processes. Added compiled component registries and framework-specific island
  hydration, and corrected generated scaffold builds.
- Upgraded Python and JavaScript dependencies and updated the Makefile upgrade workflow to use `prek update`.
- Replaced HTTP Inertia SSR configuration with development ModuleRunner and production stdio
  workers. Removed `url`, `auto_start`, `health_check`, and `health_check_timeout`;
  SSR failures now fall back to client rendering by default. See [v0.32 Migration Guide](learn/migration-0-32.md)
  for dependency, configuration, and generated-artifact migration steps.

## 0.31.0 - 2026-08-17

- Emitted configured CSRF cookie and header names (`CSRF_COOKIE_NAME` and `CSRF_HEADER_NAME`)
  as static constants in generated TypeScript route definitions (`routes.ts`) sourced from
  `app.csrf_config`. ([#353](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/issues/353))
- Added static fallback support to frontend CSRF helpers (`getCsrfHeaderName`, `getCookieToken`,
  `getCsrfToken`, `csrfHeaders`, and `csrfFetch`) so generated constants can be passed in
  non-server-rendered contexts (e.g. standalone SPA dev servers, unit tests, and API clients)
  while preserving runtime window global precedence. ([#353](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/issues/353))
- Updated dependencies and version metadata for 0.31.0.

## 0.30.1 - 2026-08-15

- Fixed static route authentication metadata emission at handler level and decoupled native static
  serving eligibility. ([#349](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/issues/349),
  [#350](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/issues/350),
  [#351](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/351))

## 0.30.0 - 2026-08-11

- Fixed direct `msgspec.Struct` Inertia handler returns to use serialized top-level field names,
  including struct `rename=` rules and explicit `msgspec.field(name=...)` aliases.
  ([#345](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/issues/345))
- Added async and synchronous `ViteAssetLoader` APIs for resolving exact secondary Vite HTML
  entries in development and their explicit artifacts in production. The paired npm endpoint safely
  reads entries beneath the configured Vite root, and optional absolute development asset URLs support
  documents opened outside the application origin. ([#346](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/issues/346))

## 0.29.1 - 2026-08-04

- Fixed relative hot-file paths being rebased against the Vite root when `bundleDir` is absolute.
  The core plugin and framework integrations now share the same resolver, so the hot file is written
  directly beneath the configured bundle directory. ([#341](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/issues/341),
  [#343](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/343))
- Fixed Vite 8.1 and newer compatibility proxies erasing HMR defaults with enumerable `undefined`
  values. HMR options now merge only defined values, explicit overrides and disable flags are preserved,
  and proxy mode lets Vite infer the browser client port from `@vite/client` instead of synthesizing a
  potentially stale Litestar port. ([#342](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/issues/342),
  [#343](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/343))
- Changed the internal Vite build and test configurations to use `import.meta.dirname` so they work
  with Vite's native config loader without compatibility warnings.
- Updated the release metadata to 0.29.1 and refreshed the Python and JavaScript dependency locks,
  including `bump-my-version` 1.5.0 and `fsspec` 2026.7.0. ([#340](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar-vite/pull/340))

## 0.29.0 - 2026-07-27

- Added `InertiaConfig.shared_page_prop_types` for typing props pushed at request time with
  `share()`. Guards and middleware have no naming site the generator can read, so `auth` and
  similar props previously fell back to a synthesized `AuthData` shape. Declared annotations are
  registered against the same OpenAPI schema registry as route props, so nested models resolve to the
  identical generated TypeScript type instead of a hand-maintained duplicate. Plain models, containers,
  and unions are all accepted. The field holds types only and never values.
- Added a generated `inertia.d.ts` that fills Inertia's `flashDataType` configuration slot with the
  generated `FlashMessages` interface, making `page.flash.success` a `string[]` rather than
  `unknown`. It is referenced from `page-props.ts` so it still applies when a `tsconfig.json`
  excludes the generated directory. `include_default_flash=False` skips it and removes any stale copy.
- Added `csrfCookieName` and `csrfHeaderName` to the `.litestar.json` bridge and injected browser
  state. `getCsrfToken()`, `getCsrfHeaderName()`, `csrfHeaders()`, `csrfFetch()`, and the HTMX
  extension now follow custom `CSRFConfig(cookie_name=..., header_name=...)` values automatically.
- Fixed `litestar assets init` failing with a bare `ModuleNotFoundError` when the `jinja` extra was
  not installed. Scaffolding now raises `MissingDependencyError` with install instructions from every
  entry point, and writes no files before failing.
- Fixed the install hints in `MissingDependencyError`. The direct-install hint named the extra instead
  of the distribution (`pip install jinja` rather than `pip install jinja2`), and storage backends
  suggested a `litestar-vite[gcsfs]`-style extra that does not exist.
- Fixed the empty generated `static-props.ts` describing itself as "currently empty" while pointing at
  `ViteConfig.static_props`. Inertia applications typically use the unrelated
  `InertiaConfig.extra_static_page_props`, so an empty file read like a generation failure.
- Fixed the Astro integration silently ignoring a user-supplied `executor`; the Nuxt and SvelteKit
  integrations already honored it. `LitestarAstroConfig` now accepts `executor` like the others.
- Fixed `AssetNotFoundError` and `ManifestNotFoundError` discarding the paths passed to them. The
  messages still omit filesystem paths, which are now available as `file_path` and `manifest_path`
  attributes.
- Changed SPA/proxy route derivation so `/api` and `/schema` are reserved only when registered
  Litestar routes, OpenAPI configuration, or `RuntimeConfig.extra_route_prefixes` claim them. Add
  `extra_route_prefixes=("/api",)` if an application relied on the old guessed fallback.
- Changed Inertia `share()` so top-level `defer()`, `optional()`, `once()`, and `always()`
  callables run only when the current response renders them or when a redirect needs to persist
  them. The `True`/`False` return contract is unchanged, and async special props still return
  `False` because they cannot be persisted synchronously across redirects.
- Changed Inertia transient state to stay request-local when the current response can consume it
  and to use the configured session automatically when state must survive a redirect. Existing
  session-backed application setup remains compatible.
- Changed `mode="external"` back to a fully supported alias of `mode="framework"`. It no longer emits
  a `DeprecationWarning`, and still requires `runtime.external_dev_server`. All five mode aliases
  (`inertia`, `htmx`, `ssr`, `ssg`, `external`) are permanent and silent.
- Changed `litestar assets doctor` to isolate each diagnostic check. A check that fails is reported as
  a warning instead of aborting the whole run.
- Changed the SPA development handler to send `text/html; charset=utf-8`, matching what the production
  handler already sent.
- Changed the per-framework `AstroTypesConfig`, `NuxtTypesConfig`, `SvelteKitTypesConfig`, and
  `TypesConfig` types into aliases of one shared definition. The names and accepted fields are
  unchanged; the integrations can no longer drift apart.
- Deprecated `materialize_shared_props_to_session()` for removal in v0.30.0; Inertia redirect
  responses now perform the compatible session handoff automatically.
- Replaced HTMX JSON-template expression evaluation with a CSP-safe allowlist interpreter. Assignment,
  `new`, functions/arrows, computed indexing, array literals, and globals other than `JSON` and
  `Math` are no longer supported. Reserved data-field names include `constructor`, `__proto__`,
  `prototype`, `apply`, `call`, `bind`, `arguments`, `callee`, `caller`, and the
  `__define*`/`__lookup*` names; rename those fields before using them in expressions.
  `@event` now exposes a sanitized `$event` wrapper instead of the raw DOM event. Applications may
  remove CSP `script-src 'unsafe-eval'` when no other code requires it.
- **Breaking**: `MissingDependencyError` takes `extra` in place of `install_package`. `extra` names
  a `litestar-vite` extra and may be omitted for dependencies that are not exposed as one.
- **Breaking**: Removed `litestar_vite.commands` and `init_vite()`. Use `litestar_vite.scaffolding`
  (`TemplateContext` plus `generate_project()`), which is what `litestar assets init` calls and
  which supports Tailwind, subdirectory output, and client/Zod generation that `init_vite()` did not.
- **Breaking**: Removed `create_ssr_proxy_controller()` and `create_ssr_websocket_handler()`,
  deprecated since 0.23.0. Use `SSRProxyMiddleware` for HTTP and `create_ssr_ws_proxy_handler()` for
  WebSocket HMR.
- **Breaking**: Removed `inject_body_content()`, `inject_json_script()`, and
  `set_element_inner_html()` from `litestar_vite.html_transform`, along with the unused
  `InertiaProps` type. `html_transform` now declares an explicit `__all__`.
- **Breaking**: `flash` and `errors` are no longer generated into `GeneratedSharedProps`. Inertia
  carries both on the page object, and the runtime has always sent them that way, so the generated types
  were the only thing that disagreed. `page.props.flash` never held a value at runtime and now fails to
  compile; read `page.flash` instead. `page.props.errors` keeps working because Inertia declares it,
  and gains the accurate `string` value type in place of the `string[]` that was generated before.
- **Breaking**: `include_default_flash` no longer emits an `auth` prop as a side effect. Applications
  running `include_default_auth=False` with `include_default_flash=True` previously received a
  generated `auth` entry anyway; set `include_default_auth=True` to keep it.

## 0.28.0 - 2026-07-25

- Added zero-dependency browser stream helpers for generic WebSocket/SSE routes,
  regular Litestar Channels routes, and Litestar Queues routes, including
  reconnect backoff, health, heartbeat filtering, deduplication, and gap
  warnings.
- Added the light-DOM `<litestar-stream>` custom element with optional JSON
  template swapping. For JSON streams it replaces `htmx-ext-ws` and
  `htmx-ext-sse` rather than layering a second reconnect policy.
- Added optional `litestar-vite-plugin/react`, `/vue`, and `/svelte`
  adapters with both generic and queue-specific bindings.
- Added a server-neutral production static-provider contract for optional Granian 0.16+ native serving while retaining Litestar's static route on every ASGI server.
- Added an explicit native/ASGI placement result with a diagnostic reason for development, framework/SSR, protected or customized assets, unsafe routes, and invalid production builds.
- Fixed Vite and Inertia SSR sidecar ownership so the Litestar server lifespan performs graceful process-group cleanup without installing competing global signal handlers.
- Fixed Vite's run-environment handling so built-in Uvicorn and Granian-backed `litestar run` commands expose the same effective host and port to frontend sidecars and the `.litestar.json` bridge.
- Changed Vite hotfile readiness so the JS plugin writes the hotfile only after the dev server is listening.
  Python now pre-writes only user-asserted `ExternalDevServer` targets, so requests arriving during Vite
  startup fall through to built assets instead of proxying to an unbound socket and returning `502`.
- Hardened Vite 8.1 HMR compatibility by emitting network options under `server.ws.*` on Vite 8.1+,
  retaining `server.hmr.*` emission for Vite 7 / 8.0, and continuing to read either shape from user
  configuration.

## 0.26.1 - 2026-07-06

- Fixed `litestar assets build` so `.litestar.json` is written before pre-build code generators and the JS typegen CLI read the Vite bridge.

## 0.26.0 - 2026-07-05

### Migration notes

- Inertia asset-version mismatches now follow the protocol more strictly: stale `GET` visits receive the `409` refresh response, while stale non-`GET` submissions continue to their handlers. Review handlers that relied on non-`GET` mismatch short-circuiting.
- Inertia infinite-scroll metadata is now emitted as `scrollProps` keyed by data prop name. Frontend code that read a single flat scroll config should read `scrollProps.<propName>` instead.
- Type generation now fails production builds by default when generation fails. Set `TypeGenConfig(fail_on_error=False)` or `types.failOnError = false` to keep warn-only build behavior.
- `litestar assets init --no-prompt` now defaults TypeScript type generation and API client generation ON (previously off). Pass the new `--no-enable-types` or `--no-generate-client` flags to restore the previous behavior non-interactively.
- `litestar assets init --no-prompt` now aborts with exit code `2` when scaffold files (e.g. `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`) already exist, instead of proceeding and skipping them. Pass `--overwrite` to proceed non-interactively.

- Fixed Inertia asset-version mismatch handling so only `GET` requests can return the protocol `409` refresh response; non-GET submissions now continue to their handlers instead of being downgraded and losing the request body. (#306)
- Fixed `share()` with Inertia redirects so top-level sync special props are materialized before session storage and async special props are skipped instead of crashing session serialization. (#306)
- Fixed request-scope Inertia shared props so they are still rendered on routes without session middleware.
- Fixed Inertia infinite-scroll `scrollProps` to emit a record keyed by data prop name, matching the official client protocol. (#306)
- Fixed explicit Inertia `scroll_props=` responses so metadata is keyed by the returned data prop when there is a single route prop.
- Fixed auto-wrapped Inertia responses so non-Inertia JSON handlers preserve Litestar's resolved `201`/`204` status codes while user-created `InertiaResponse` statuses still win. (#306)
- Fixed Precognition validation success handling for handlers without an explicit `request` parameter by using the middleware request context. (#306)
- Fixed Inertia SSR serialization so app, handler, and response type encoders are honored for custom page prop values. (#306)
- Fixed Inertia partial reloads so `deferredProps` metadata is omitted on partial responses while initial responses still advertise deferred props. (#306)
- Fixed Inertia partial reloads so plain dict route props honor `X-Inertia-Partial-Data` and `X-Inertia-Partial-Except` independently.
- Fixed `litestar assets init` so generated `package.json` files no longer emit duplicate dependency keys. (#302, #303)
- Fixed type generation so the JS plugin resolves local `@hey-api/openapi-ts` installs first, uses a pinned package-manager fallback when needed, fails production builds loudly by default, and lets `TypeGenConfig(fail_on_error=False)` or `types.failOnError = false` opt out. (#311, #314)
- Fixed Deno type-generation fallback execution when the providing npm package exposes a binary with a different name.
- Fixed type generation reliability for generated outputs by preserving queued dev regenerations, checking that expected output files exist before reusing caches, watching `routes.json`, emitting `static-props.ts` from the shared CLI path, and handling semantic aliases and nested hey-api operation types. (#311, #314)
- Fixed Vite dev-server resilience by revalidating hotfile targets by mtime, recovering after missing or replaced hotfiles, tolerating additive/corrupt bridge config files, aligning TLS certificate env vars, and preserving static-files defaults when user overrides leave fields unset. (#312, #314)
- Fixed `litestar assets init` scaffold correctness for framework variants without dedicated directories, Tailwind CSS/PostCSS dependencies and entry inputs, current hey-api/TanStack/Vite template APIs, transactional writes, and non-interactive collision handling. (#313, #314)
- Updated npm publishing to use trusted publishing with provenance and no npm token. (#314)
- Fixed Vite dev-server lifecycle handling so unexpected exits are restarted with capped backoff and intentional shutdowns do not trigger restarts. (#317)
- Fixed Vite dev-server auto-restart so each recovered crash gets a fresh retry budget instead of exhausting the lifetime budget.
- Changed SPA/proxy route-prefix fallbacks so `/docs` is no longer reserved unless Litestar actually registers docs there or `RuntimeConfig.extra_route_prefixes` includes it. (#317)
- Added `ViteConfig(enabled=...)` and `VITE_ENABLED` so Vite routes and lifespans can be disabled in CLI, worker, and test contexts while keeping asset CLI commands available. (#301, #310)
- Added `RuntimeConfig.extra_route_prefixes` for deliberately reserving custom backend prefixes from SPA/proxy fallbacks. (#317)
- Added `--no-enable-types` and `--no-generate-client` opt-out flags to `litestar assets init` so `--no-prompt` runs can disable TypeScript type generation and API client generation non-interactively.
- Fixed `getCsrfToken()` so SPA and HTMX helpers can fall back to the `csrftoken` or `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie when injected page-state sources are absent. (#299, #310)
- Hardened HTMX helper handling so dynamic `href`, `src`, and `action` attributes reject dangerous protocols and expression checks catch denied globals reconstructed through string concatenation. (#316)
- Simplified Vite integration internals by consolidating type-config resolution, hotfile handling, proxy helpers, Inertia prop wrappers, and typing-only helper paths without removing public exports. (#316)
- Reduced duplicate work in type generation, route metadata extraction, proxy header filtering, deploy diffing, bridge reads, placeholder probing, and Inertia response wrapping while preserving generated output paths and public behavior. (#315)
- Fixed SPA startup so async lifespan initialization uses the async handler path and custom Inertia component option keys are preserved when startup wrappers are installed. (#315)
- Fixed production SPA manifest resolution for Vite's default `.vite/manifest.json` path and recursive deploy change detection for nested bundle assets. (#315)
- Updated Python dependencies: `typing-extensions` 4.16.0, `prek` 0.4.8, `slotscheck` 0.20.1, and `coverage` 7.15.0. (#309)

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/angular.md -->

# Angular

Litestar supports two integration approaches for Angular applications:

1. **Vite-Based (`angular` template, `mode="spa"`)** — Uses `@analogjs/vite-plugin-angular` directly with `litestar-vite-plugin` for single-port HMR and unified Vite builds.
2. **Angular CLI (`angular-cli` template, `mode="external"`)** — Uses the native Angular CLI (`ng serve` / `ng build` via `@angular/build:application`) with `ExternalDevServer` process management and `TypeGenConfig`.

---

## Comparison: Vite vs Angular CLI

| Feature | Option 1: Vite (`@analogjs/vite-plugin-angular`) | Option 2: Angular CLI (`@angular/build`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Scaffold Template** | `litestar assets init --template angular` | `litestar assets init --template angular-cli` |
| **Operating Mode** | `mode="spa"` | `mode="external"` |
| **Build Tool** | Vite (`litestar-vite-plugin`) | Angular CLI (`angular.json` + `@angular/build:application`) |
| **Dev Server** | Vite HMR proxied through Litestar (`:8000`) | `ng serve` managed via `ExternalDevServer` |
| **Type Generation** | Automatic via `litestar-vite-plugin` | Automatic via `ViteConfig(types=TypeGenConfig(...))` |
| **Best For** | New fullstack projects wanting unified Vite tooling | Existing Angular CLI workspaces or enterprise `ng` pipelines |

---

## Vite-Based Angular

### Quick Start

```bash
litestar assets init --template angular
litestar assets install
litestar run --reload
```

### Configuration

=== "Python (`app.py`)"

    ```python title="app.py"
    from pathlib import Path

    from litestar import Litestar, get
    from msgspec import Struct
    from litestar_vite import PathConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


    class Book(Struct):
        id: int
        title: str
        author: str


    @get("/api/books", name="books", sync_to_thread=False)
    def list_books() -> list[Book]:
        """Return typed book catalog."""
        return [Book(id=1, title="Async Python", author="Litestar Team")]


    app = Litestar(
        route_handlers=[list_books],
        plugins=[
            VitePlugin(
                config=ViteConfig(
                    mode="spa",
                    dev_mode=True,
                    paths=PathConfig(resource_dir=Path("src")),
                    types=TypeGenConfig(generate_sdk=True, generate_routes=True),
                ),
            ),
        ],
    )
    ```

=== "Vite (`vite.config.ts`)"

    <!-- docs-example: skip -->
    ```typescript title="vite.config.ts"
    import { defineConfig } from "vite";
    import angular from "@analogjs/vite-plugin-angular";
    import litestar from "litestar-vite-plugin";

    export default defineConfig({
      plugins: [
        angular(),
        litestar({
          input: ["src/main.ts"],
          types: "auto",
        }),
      ],
    });
    ```

### Standalone Component with `HttpClient` and `route`

```typescript title="src/app/books.component.ts"
import { Component, inject, type OnInit } from "@angular/core";
import { HttpClient } from "@angular/common/http";
import { route } from "../generated/routes";
import type { Book } from "../generated/api";

@Component({
  selector: "app-books",
  standalone: true,
  template: `
    <section>
      <h2>Books</h2>
      <ul>
        @for (book of books; track book.id) {
          <li>{{ book.title }} — {{ book.author }}</li>
        }
      </ul>
    </section>
  `,
})
export class BooksComponent implements OnInit {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);
  books: Book[] = [];

  ngOnInit(): void {
    this.http.get<Book[]>(route("books")).subscribe((data) => {
      this.books = data;
    });
  }
}
```

---

## Angular CLI

When using Angular CLI (`@angular/build:application` and `@angular/build:dev-server`), configure `mode="external"` and `ExternalDevServer` so `litestar run` starts `ng serve` and proxies non-API traffic automatically:

```bash
litestar assets init --template angular-cli
litestar assets install
litestar run --reload
```

```python title="app.py"
from pathlib import Path

from litestar import Litestar
from litestar_vite import ExternalDevServer, PathConfig, RuntimeConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin

app = Litestar(
    route_handlers=[],
    plugins=[
        VitePlugin(
            config=ViteConfig(
                mode="external",
                dev_mode=True,
                paths=PathConfig(bundle_dir=Path("dist/browser")),
                runtime=RuntimeConfig(
                    external_dev_server=ExternalDevServer(
                        target="http://127.0.0.1:4200",
                        command=["npx", "ng", "serve", "--port", "4200"],
                        build_command=["npx", "ng", "build"],
                    ),
                ),
                types=TypeGenConfig(
                    output=Path("src/generated"),
                    generate_sdk=True,
                    generate_routes=True,
                ),
            ),
        ),
    ],
)
```

# Astro

Pair [Astro](https://astro.build) with Litestar using `litestar-vite-plugin/astro` (`mode="ssg"` or `mode="framework"`) to build content-focused sites with Islands Architecture, file-based routing, and end-to-end OpenAPI + route type generation.

---

## Quick Start

```bash
litestar assets init --template astro
litestar assets install
litestar run --reload
```

---

## Project Structure

```text
my-project/
├── app.py                  # Litestar API + ViteConfig(mode="ssg")
├── astro.config.mjs        # Astro config with litestar() integration
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
└── src/
    ├── pages/
    │   └── index.astro     # Astro pages with frontmatter data fetching
    ├── layouts/
    │   └── Layout.astro
    └── generated/          # Auto-generated routes.ts, schemas.ts, api/
```

---

## Configuration

=== "Python (`app.py`)"

    ```python title="app.py"
    from pathlib import Path

    from litestar import Litestar, get
    from msgspec import Struct
    from litestar_vite import PathConfig, RuntimeConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


    class Book(Struct):
        id: int
        title: str
        author: str


    @get("/api/books", name="books", sync_to_thread=False)
    def list_books() -> list[Book]:
        """Return typed book list for Astro pages."""
        return [Book(id=1, title="Astro + Litestar", author="Litestar Team")]


    app = Litestar(
        route_handlers=[list_books],
        plugins=[
            VitePlugin(
                config=ViteConfig(
                    mode="ssg",
                    dev_mode=True,
                    paths=PathConfig(resource_dir=Path("src"), bundle_dir=Path("dist")),
                    runtime=RuntimeConfig(executor="node"),
                    types=TypeGenConfig(output=Path("src/generated"), generate_sdk=True, generate_routes=True),
                ),
            ),
        ],
    )
    ```

=== "Astro (`astro.config.mjs`)"

    ```typescript title="astro.config.mjs"
    import { defineConfig } from "astro/config";
    import litestar from "litestar-vite-plugin/astro";

    export default defineConfig({
      integrations: [
        litestar({
          apiPrefix: "/api",
          types: true,
        }),
      ],
    });
    ```

---

## How the Astro Integration Works

1. **Bridge & Hotfile Sync**: Reads `.litestar.json` on startup and writes the active Astro dev server URL to the `hot` file (`dist/hot`) so Litestar's single-port `ViteProxyMiddleware` routes non-API requests to Astro automatically.
2. **Dev Proxy**: Configures Vite's `server.proxy` for `apiPrefix` (default `"/api"`) so direct visits to Astro's port also forward API requests to Litestar.
3. **Automatic Codegen**: Runs `@hey-api/openapi-ts` when `openapi.json` or `routes.json` change.

---

## Fetching Typed Data in Astro Pages

Import `route()` and OpenAPI types directly inside Astro's server frontmatter fence (`---`):

```astro title="src/pages/index.astro"
---
import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
import { route } from "../generated/routes";
import type { Book } from "../generated/api";

const apiOrigin = import.meta.env.PUBLIC_API_URL || "http://127.0.0.1:8000";
const response = await fetch(`${apiOrigin}${route("books")}`);
const books: Book[] = await response.json();
---

<Layout title="Catalog">
  <main>
    <h1>Books</h1>
    <ul>
      {books.map((book) => (
        <li><strong>{book.title}</strong> — {book.author}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  </main>
</Layout>
```

---

## Rendering Modes & Interactive Islands

| Astro Output Mode | Litestar `ViteConfig(mode=...)` | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `output: "static"` (default) | `mode="ssg"` | `litestar assets build` compiles static HTML into `dist/`; Litestar serves static pages and `/api/*` in production. |
| `output: "server"` | `mode="ssr"` | Astro runs a Node/Deno adapter for dynamic SSR; combine with React/Vue/Svelte `client:load` or `client:visible` islands. |

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/htmx.md -->

# HTMX

Combine Litestar's server-rendered Jinja2 templates (`litestar-htmx`) with Vite asset bundling, CSRF header injection, client-side JSON templating (`hx-swap="json"`), and declarative `<litestar-stream>` updates.

---

## Quick Start

```bash
litestar assets init --template htmx
litestar assets install
litestar run --reload
```

---

## Project Structure

```text
my-project/
├── app.py                  # Litestar + VitePlugin(mode="htmx") + HTMXPlugin
├── package.json
├── vite.config.ts
├── resources/
│   ├── main.ts             # Imports htmx.org + registerHtmxExtension()
│   └── styles.css
└── templates/
    ├── base.html.j2        # Layout with vite_hmr(), vite(), csrf-token, hx-ext="litestar"
    ├── index.html.j2       # Full page template
    └── partials/
        └── item.html.j2    # HTMX partial fragment
```

---

## Configuration

=== "Python (`app.py`)"

    <!-- docs-example: skip -->
    ```python title="app.py"
    from pathlib import Path

    from litestar import Litestar, get, post
    from litestar.contrib.jinja import JinjaTemplateEngine
    from litestar.plugins.htmx import HTMXPlugin, HTMXRequest, HTMXTemplate
    from litestar.response import Template
    from litestar.template.config import TemplateConfig
    from litestar_vite import PathConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


    @get("/", sync_to_thread=False)
    def index() -> Template:
        """Render main HTMX page."""
        return Template(template_name="index.html.j2", context={"items": ["Task A", "Task B"]})


    @post("/items", sync_to_thread=False)
    def add_item(request: HTMXRequest, data: dict[str, str]) -> Template:
        """Return partial HTML fragment for HTMX swap."""
        item = data.get("name", "New Task")
        if request.htmx:
            return HTMXTemplate(template_name="partials/item.html.j2", context={"item": item})
        return Template(template_name="index.html.j2", context={"items": [item]})


    app = Litestar(
        route_handlers=[index, add_item],
        Request=HTMXRequest,
        plugins=[
            VitePlugin(
                config=ViteConfig(
                    mode="htmx",
                    dev_mode=True,
                    paths=PathConfig(resource_dir=Path("resources")),
                ),
            ),
            HTMXPlugin(),
        ],
        template_config=TemplateConfig(
            directory=Path("templates"),
            engine=JinjaTemplateEngine,
        ),
    )
    ```

=== "Frontend Entry (`resources/main.ts`)"

    <!-- docs-example: skip -->
    ```typescript title="resources/main.ts"
    import "htmx.org";
    import { registerHtmxExtension } from "litestar-vite-plugin/helpers";
    import "./styles.css";

    // Registers the "litestar" HTMX extension:
    // 1. Automatically attaches X-CSRF-Token to non-GET HTMX requests
    // 2. Enables hx-swap="json" client-side <template> rendering
    registerHtmxExtension();
    ```

=== "Base Template (`templates/base.html.j2`)"

    ```html title="templates/base.html.j2"
    <!doctype html>
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8" />
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
        <meta name="csrf-token" content="{{ csrf_token }}" />
        <title>Litestar + HTMX</title>
        {{ vite_hmr() }}
        {{ vite('resources/main.ts') }}
      </head>
      <body hx-ext="litestar">
        {% block content %}{% endblock %}
      </body>
    </html>
    ```

---

## Client-Side JSON Templating

When an endpoint returns JSON instead of HTML, the `litestar` HTMX extension (`registerHtmxExtension()`) lets you render JSON directly into a `<template>` element using `hx-swap="json"`:

```html title="templates/index.html.j2"
<button hx-get="/api/books" hx-target="#book-list" hx-swap="json">
  Load Books from JSON API
</button>

<div id="book-list">
  <ul>
    <template ls-for="book in $data">
      <li>
        <strong ls-text="book.title"></strong> by <span ls-text="book.author"></span>
        <span ls-show="book.featured" class="badge">Featured</span>
      </li>
    </template>
  </ul>
</div>
```

### Supported Directive Grammar

| Directive | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<template ls-for="item in expr">` (or `ls-each`) | Repeat `<template>` content for each item in an array | `<template ls-for="row in $data.items">` |
| `<template ls-if="expr">` / `<template ls-else>` | Conditional `<template>` structural rendering | `<template ls-if="item.active">` |
| `ls-show="expr"` / `ls-hide="expr"` | Toggle `style.display` visibility on any element | `ls-show="item.featured"` |
| `ls-scope="expr"` | Narrow evaluation context for descendant elements | `ls-scope="item.author"` |
| `ls-text="expr"` / `${expr}` | Safe `textContent` binding or text-node interpolation | `ls-text="item.name"`, `<h3>${item.name}</h3>` |
| `ls-html="expr"` | Sanitized `innerHTML` content binding | `ls-html="item.summaryHtml"` |
| `:attr="expr"` | Dynamic attribute or `:class` object binding (`boolean` toggles presence) | `:href="item.url"`, `:disabled="!item.ready"` |
| `@event="expr"` | Event listener expression with wrapped `$event` context | `@click="selected = item.id"` |

!!! important
    **Security Model**: `registerHtmxExtension()` evaluates directive expressions using a restricted property-path and comparison parser — never `eval()` or `new Function()`. Arbitrary function calls and prototype-chain properties (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`) are blocked.

---

## Declarative Realtime Streams

Pair HTMX templates with `<litestar-stream>` (`defineStreamElement()`) to append or replace live SSE/WebSocket events without writing custom JavaScript glue. See [Realtime Event Streams](../typegen/event-streams.md) for full details.

---

# Web Frameworks

Litestar Vite supports every major frontend UI library, hypermedia library, and meta-framework while keeping Litestar as your single source of truth for routing, authentication, and data serialization.

---

## Supported Frameworks Matrix

| Framework | Mode | Integration & Helpers | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Inertia.js** | `hybrid` (`inertia`) | `litestar-vite-plugin`, `inertia-pages.json` | [Inertia Guide](inertia/index.md) |
| **React** | `spa` / `hybrid` / `template` | `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `litestar-vite-plugin/react` | [React Guide](react.md) |
| **Vue 3** | `spa` / `hybrid` / `template` | `@vitejs/plugin-vue`, `litestar-vite-plugin/vue` | [Vue 3 Guide](vue.md) |
| **Svelte 5** | `spa` / `hybrid` / `template` | `@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte`, `litestar-vite-plugin/svelte` | [Svelte 5 Guide](svelte.md) |
| **Angular** | `spa` / `external` | `litestar-vite-plugin` or `@angular/build` | [Angular Guide](angular.md) |
| **HTMX** | `template` (`htmx`) | `litestar-vite-plugin`, `<litestar-stream>` | [HTMX Guide](htmx.md) |
| **Astro** | `ssg` (`framework`) | `litestar-vite-plugin/astro` | [Astro Guide](astro.md) |
| **Nuxt** | `ssr` (`framework`) | `litestar-vite-plugin/nuxt` | [Nuxt Guide](nuxt.md) |
| **SvelteKit** | `ssr` (`framework`) | `litestar-vite-plugin/sveltekit` | [SvelteKit Guide](sveltekit.md) |

---

## Choosing a Architecture Pattern

### Server-Driven Single-Page Apps

Pair **React**, **Vue 3**, or **Svelte 5** with **Inertia.js** (`mode="hybrid"`) when you want a rich single-page frontend without maintaining a separate REST API layer, client router, or state store. Litestar route handlers return typed Python models (`msgspec.Struct`, `dataclass`, Pydantic) directly to your page components.

- [→ Inertia.js Overview](inertia/index.md)

### Client-Routed SPAs

Use **React**, **Vue 3**, **Svelte 5**, or **Angular** in `mode="spa"` when your frontend uses a client-side router (`react-router`, TanStack Router, `vue-router`, `@angular/router`) and communicates with Litestar over JSON API endpoints using the generated `@hey-api/openapi-ts` SDK.

- [→ React](react.md) · [Vue 3](vue.md) · [Svelte 5](svelte.md) · [Angular](angular.md)

### Server Templates, HTMX & Island Fragments

Use **HTMX** and Jinja2 templates (`mode="template"` or `mode="htmx"`) when HTML lives on the server, optionally embedding interactive `<litestar-island>` components rendered by React, Vue, or Svelte.

- [→ HTMX Guide](htmx.md) · [Islands & Fragment Architecture](../learn/islands-and-htmx.md)

### Meta-Frameworks

Use **Astro**, **Nuxt**, or **SvelteKit** when you want file-based routing, static site generation (SSG), or meta-framework SSR while Litestar serves your `/api/*`, `/schema/*`, and WebSocket routes through a single-port proxy.

- [→ Astro](astro.md) · [Nuxt](nuxt.md) · [SvelteKit](sveltekit.md)

---
