<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/client-visits.md -->

# Polling, Prefetching & Remembering State

Inertia provides built-in client hooks for periodic background polling (`usePoll`), link prefetching (`<Link prefetch>`), and preserving local component/form state across browser history navigation (`useRemember`).

---

## Periodic Polling

Use `usePoll(intervalMs, requestOptions, pollOptions)` to refresh specific props on an interval. By default, Inertia throttles polling automatically when the browser tab is in the background (`keepAlive: false`) and cleans up the timer when the component unmounts:

=== "React"

    <!-- docs-example: skip -->
    ```tsx title="resources/pages/System/Status.tsx"
    import { usePoll } from "@inertiajs/react";

    export default function SystemStatus({ metrics }: { metrics: { cpu: number; jobs: number } }) {
      const { start, stop } = usePoll(
        5000,
        { only: ["metrics"] },
        { keepAlive: false, autoStart: true },
      );

      return (
        <section>
          <p>CPU: {metrics.cpu}% | Active Jobs: {metrics.jobs}</p>
          <button type="button" onClick={stop}>Pause Polling</button>
          <button type="button" onClick={start}>Resume Polling</button>
        </section>
      );
    }
    ```

=== "Vue 3"

    <!-- docs-example: skip -->
    ```vue title="resources/pages/System/Status.vue"
    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { usePoll } from "@inertiajs/vue3";

    defineProps<{ metrics: { cpu: number; jobs: number } }>();

    const { start, stop } = usePoll(
      5000,
      { only: ["metrics"] },
      { keepAlive: false, autoStart: true },
    );
    </script>

    <template>
      <section>
        <p>CPU: {{ metrics.cpu }}% | Active Jobs: {{ metrics.jobs }}</p>
        <button type="button" @click="stop">Pause Polling</button>
        <button type="button" @click="start">Resume Polling</button>
      </section>
    </template>
    ```

!!! tip
    On the server, wrap props targeted by `usePoll(..., { only: ["metrics"] })` in `lazy("metrics", load_metrics)` or keep unrelated heavy props in `once()` so each 5-second poll executes only the lightweight metrics query.

---

## Link Prefetching

Add `prefetch` to `<Link>` components to warm the client cache before the user clicks:

| Strategy | Usage | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hover (Default)** | `<Link href="/users" prefetch>` or `prefetch="hover"` | Prefetches after the user hovers over the link for >75ms. |
| **Mount** | `<Link href="/dashboard" prefetch="mount">` | Prefetches immediately when the link mounts into the DOM. |
| **Click (Mouse Down)** | `<Link href="/reports" prefetch="click">` | Starts fetching on `mousedown` before `mouseup` completes. |
| **Custom Cache TTL** | `<Link href="/users" prefetch cacheFor="1m">` | Controls how long the prefetched `PageProps` remain fresh (default 30s). |

You can also prefetch programmatically via `router.prefetch(route("users.index"), { method: "get" }, { cacheFor: "30s" })` or invalidate cached pages after a mutation with `router.flushAll()`.

---

## Remembering Local State

When a user types into a search filter or switches tabs and then clicks a link and presses the browser **Back** button, standard component state resets. `useRemember` automatically serializes local state into `window.history.state` and restores it on history navigation:

=== "React"

    <!-- docs-example: skip -->
    ```tsx title="resources/pages/Orders/FilterBar.tsx"
    import { useRemember } from "@inertiajs/react";

    export function FilterBar() {
      const [filters, setFilters] = useRemember(
        { search: "", status: "all", showArchived: false },
        "Orders/FilterBar",
      );

      return (
        <input
          value={filters.search}
          onChange={(e) => setFilters({ ...filters, search: e.target.value })}
          placeholder="Search orders..."
        />
      );
    }
    ```

=== "Vue 3"

    <!-- docs-example: skip -->
    ```vue title="resources/pages/Orders/FilterBar.vue"
    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { useRemember } from "@inertiajs/vue3";

    const filters = useRemember(
      { search: "", status: "all", showArchived: false },
      "Orders/FilterBar",
    );
    </script>

    <template>
      <input v-model="filters.search" placeholder="Search orders..." />
    </template>
    ```

### Remembering Form State

Pass a unique storage key as the first argument to `useForm("CreateUserForm", { name: "", email: "" })` to automatically remember unsaved form inputs and validation errors across Back/Forward history navigation.

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/configuration-and-templates.md -->

# Configuration & Root Templates

Setting `ViteConfig(mode="hybrid")` (or `mode="inertia"`) enables Inertia support automatically. You can customize every aspect of the protocol by passing an [`InertiaConfig`](../../reference/plugin-and-config.md#litestar_vite.config.InertiaConfig) instance (or `inertia=True` for defaults) to `ViteConfig`.

---

## Inertia Configuration

```python title="app.py"
from litestar import Litestar
from litestar.middleware.session.server_side import ServerSideSessionConfig
from litestar_vite import InertiaConfig, InertiaSSRConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin
from litestar_vite.config import InertiaTypeGenConfig, SPAConfig

app = Litestar(
    route_handlers=[],
    middleware=[ServerSideSessionConfig().middleware],
    plugins=[
        VitePlugin(
            config=ViteConfig(
                mode="hybrid",
                spa=SPAConfig(app_selector="#app"),
                inertia=InertiaConfig(
                    root_template="index.html.j2",
                    redirect_unauthorized_to="/login",
                    redirect_404="/404",
                    encrypt_history=False,
                    use_script_element=True,
                    precognition=True,
                    ssr=InertiaSSRConfig(enabled=True, timeout=5.0),
                    type_gen=InertiaTypeGenConfig(
                        include_default_auth=True,
                        include_default_flash=True,
                    ),
                ),
                types=TypeGenConfig(generate_page_props=True),
            ),
        ),
    ],
)
```

### Key Configuration Options

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `root_template` | `"index.html"` | Root HTML or Jinja2 template rendered on initial full-page Inertia visits. |
| `component_opt_keys` | `("component", "page")` | Route handler `opt` keys inspected to determine the Inertia page component name. |
| `use_script_element` | `True` | Emit initial page JSON inside `<script type="application/json" id="app_page" data-page="app">` instead of an HTML-escaped `data-page` attribute. |
| `app_selector` | `"#app"` | CSS ID selector for the root mount container (`#app`, `#root`). |
| `encrypt_history` | `False` | Globally enable browser `window.history.state` encryption via Web Crypto. |
| `precognition` | `False` | Register the Laravel Precognition validation exception handler (422 / 204). |
| `redirect_unauthorized_to` | `None` | Automatically redirect unauthenticated (401) Inertia requests to this path. |
| `redirect_404` | `None` | Automatically redirect 404 Not Found Inertia requests to this path. |
| `extra_static_page_props` | `{}` | Static key-value dictionary merged into every Inertia response's `props`. |
| `extra_session_page_props` | `set()` | Session keys automatically read from `request.session` and merged into `props`. |
| `shared_page_prop_types` | `{}` | Mapping of shared prop keys to Python types (`{"auth": AuthProp}`) for `page-props.ts` codegen. |
| `ssr` | `False` | `bool` or [`InertiaSSRConfig`](../../reference/plugin-and-config.md#litestar_vite.config.InertiaSSRConfig) enabling server-side rendering. |

---

## Vite Plugin Boundary

In Litestar Vite projects, **`litestar-vite-plugin` is the sole Vite bridge owner**. Do **not** install `@inertiajs/vite` alongside `litestar-vite-plugin`:

- `litestar-vite-plugin` auto-detects Inertia mode from `.litestar.json` (`mode: "hybrid"` or `mode: "template"` with Inertia enabled).
- It manages the `hot` file, `/__litestar_ssr__` dev SSR endpoint, React Fast Refresh preamble, and type generation without conflicting middleware.

---

## Root Templates: SPA Mode vs Jinja2 Template Mode

Inertia works in two HTML shell modes:

=== "Hybrid SPA Shell"

    In `mode="hybrid"` without `TemplateConfig`, Litestar reads your plain `index.html` (from the project root or `resources/index.html`) and transforms it at runtime — injecting the Vite HMR client, module scripts, and the `<script type="application/json" id="app_page" data-page="app">` payload around `<div id="app"></div>`:

    ```html title="index.html"
    <!doctype html>
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8" />
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
        <title>My Inertia App</title>
      </head>
      <body>
        <div id="app"></div>
        <script type="module" src="/resources/main.tsx"></script>
      </body>
    </html>
    ```

=== "Jinja2 Template"

    When you configure Litestar's `TemplateConfig(engine=JinjaTemplateEngine)`, `InertiaResponse` renders `root_template` through Jinja2 using the `vite_hmr()`, `vite()`, and `inertia` template callables:

    ```html title="templates/index.html.j2"
    <!doctype html>
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8" />
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
        <title>My Inertia App</title>
        {{ vite_hmr() }}
        {{ vite('resources/main.tsx') }}
      </head>
      <body>
        {{ inertia }}
      </body>
    </html>
    ```

---

## Script-Element Initial Page Bootstrap

By default, `InertiaConfig(use_script_element=True)` serializes initial page props into `<script type="application/json" id="app_page" data-page="app">{...}</script><div id="app"></div>` rather than an HTML-escaped `data-page="&quot;...&quot;"` attribute. This cuts initial HTML payload size by ~30% and avoids HTML entity decoding overhead.

- **Standard Inertia clients** enable script-element parsing by setting `defaults: { future: { useScriptElementForInitialPage: true } }` in `createInertiaApp(...)`.
- **Inertia v3 clients** read the `<script type="application/json" data-page="app">` element automatically with `defaults: {}`:

=== "Standard Client"

    ```tsx title="resources/main.tsx"
    import { createInertiaApp } from "@inertiajs/react";
    import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
    import { resolvePageComponent } from "litestar-vite-plugin/inertia-helpers";

    createInertiaApp({
      defaults: {
        future: {
          useScriptElementForInitialPage: true,
        },
      },
      resolve: (name: string) =>
        resolvePageComponent(`./pages/${name}.tsx`, import.meta.glob("./pages/**/*.tsx")),
      setup({ el, App, props }: { el: HTMLElement; App: any; props: any }) {
        createRoot(el).render(<App {...props} />);
      },
    });
    ```

=== "Inertia v3 Client"

    ```tsx title="resources/main.tsx"
    import { createInertiaApp } from "@inertiajs/react";
    import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
    import { csrfHeaders } from "litestar-vite-plugin/helpers";
    import { resolvePageComponent } from "litestar-vite-plugin/inertia-helpers";

    createInertiaApp({
      defaults: {
        visitOptions: (_href: string, options: { headers?: Record<string, string> }) => ({
          headers: csrfHeaders(options.headers ?? {}),
        }),
      },
      resolve: (name: string) =>
        resolvePageComponent(`./pages/${name}.tsx`, import.meta.glob("./pages/**/*.tsx")),
      setup({ el, App, props }: { el: HTMLElement; App: any; props: any }) {
        createRoot(el).render(<App {...props} />);
      },
    });
    ```

!!! note
    If you prefer the legacy `data-page="..."` attribute on `<div id="app">`, set `InertiaConfig(use_script_element=False)`.

---

## Custom Mount Selector & Multiple Root Templates

- **Custom Mount Container**: If your frontend mounts to `#root` instead of `#app`, set `InertiaConfig(app_selector="#root")`. Litestar automatically emits `<script type="application/json" id="root_page" data-page="root">` and `<div id="root"></div>`.
- **Per-Route Template Override**: Pass `template_name="admin.html.j2"` to `InertiaResponse(..., template_name="admin.html.j2")` when specific route groups need a distinct HTML shell.

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/file-uploads.md -->

# File Uploads

Inertia's `useForm` and `router` automatically detect `File` or `Blob` objects anywhere inside your form data (including nested objects and arrays), convert the request payload into `multipart/form-data`, and emit real-time upload progress events.

---

## Handling File Uploads in Litestar

Use Litestar's `RequestEncodingType.MULTI_PART` and `UploadFile` (or `list[UploadFile]`) inside a `msgspec.Struct` or dataclass to accept single or multiple file uploads alongside regular form fields:

```python title="app.py"
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, Any

from litestar import Request, post
from litestar.datastructures import UploadFile
from litestar.enums import RequestEncodingType
from litestar.params import Body
from msgspec import Struct
from litestar_vite.inertia import InertiaRedirect, flash


class UpdateAvatarPayload(Struct):
    display_name: str
    avatar: UploadFile


class UploadDocumentsPayload(Struct):
    folder: str
    documents: list[UploadFile]


@post("/profile/avatar", name="profile.avatar", sync_to_thread=False)
async def update_avatar(
    request: Request[Any, Any, Any],
    data: Annotated[UpdateAvatarPayload, Body(media_type=RequestEncodingType.MULTI_PART)],
) -> InertiaRedirect:
    """Read uploaded avatar bytes and redirect back to profile."""
    content = await data.avatar.read()
    target = Path("uploads") / (data.avatar.filename or "avatar.png")
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_bytes(content)

    flash(request, f"Uploaded avatar for {data.display_name} ({len(content)} bytes)", category="success")
    return InertiaRedirect(request, redirect_to="/profile")
```

---

## Frontend File Inputs, Previews & Progress Bars

`form.progress` provides `{ percentage, loaded, total }` while a multipart upload is in flight:

=== "React"

    ```tsx title="resources/pages/Profile/AvatarForm.tsx"
    import { type ChangeEvent, type FormEvent, useState } from "react";
    import { useForm } from "@inertiajs/react";
    import { route } from "@/generated/routes";

    export function AvatarForm({ currentName }: { currentName: string }) {
      const [previewUrl, setPreviewUrl] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const form = useForm<{ display_name: string; avatar: File | null }>({
        display_name: currentName,
        avatar: null,
      });

      function onFileChange(e: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) {
        const file = e.target.files?.[0] ?? null;
        form.setData("avatar", file);
        if (previewUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(previewUrl);
        setPreviewUrl(file ? URL.createObjectURL(file) : null);
      }

      function onSubmit(e: FormEvent) {
        e.preventDefault();
        form.post(route("profile.avatar"), {
          forceFormData: true,
        });
      }

      return (
        <form onSubmit={onSubmit}>
          <input
            value={form.data.display_name}
            onChange={(e) => form.setData("display_name", e.target.value)}
          />
          <input type="file" accept="image/*" onChange={onFileChange} />

          {previewUrl && <img src={previewUrl} alt="Avatar preview" width={96} height={96} />}

          {form.progress && (
            <progress value={form.progress.percentage} max={100}>
              {form.progress.percentage}%
            </progress>
          )}

          <button type="submit" disabled={form.processing}>
            Save Avatar
          </button>
        </form>
      );
    }
    ```

=== "Vue 3"

    ```vue title="resources/pages/Profile/AvatarForm.vue"
    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { ref } from "vue";
    import { useForm } from "@inertiajs/vue3";
    import { route } from "@/generated/routes";

    const props = defineProps<{ currentName: string }>();
    const previewUrl = ref<string | null>(null);

    const form = useForm<{ display_name: string; avatar: File | null }>({
      display_name: props.currentName,
      avatar: null,
    });

    function onFileChange(event: Event) {
      const input = event.target as HTMLInputElement;
      const file = input.files?.[0] ?? null;
      form.avatar = file;
      if (previewUrl.value) URL.revokeObjectURL(previewUrl.value);
      previewUrl.value = file ? URL.createObjectURL(file) : null;
    }

    function submit() {
      form.post(route("profile.avatar"), { forceFormData: true });
    }
    </script>

    <template>
      <form @submit.prevent="submit">
        <input v-model="form.display_name" />
        <input type="file" accept="image/*" @change="onFileChange" />

        <img v-if="previewUrl" :src="previewUrl" alt="Avatar preview" width="96" height="96" />

        <progress v-if="form.progress" :value="form.progress.percentage" max="100">
          {{ form.progress.percentage }}%
        </progress>

        <button type="submit" :disabled="form.processing">Save Avatar</button>
      </form>
    </template>
    ```

---

## Multipart Updates with PUT and PATCH

When updating a resource that includes a file upload, prefer `POST` (or pass `_method: "put"` if using method spoofing) with `forceFormData: true` so the browser encodes the payload as `multipart/form-data`.

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/forms-and-validation.md -->

# Forms, Validation & Live Precognition

Inertia includes a reactive `useForm` helper that tracks form state, submission progress, processing status, and field-level validation errors returned by Litestar.

---

## Submitting Forms with useForm

=== "React"

    ```tsx title="resources/pages/Users/Create.tsx"
    import type { FormEvent } from "react";
    import { useForm } from "@inertiajs/react";
    import { route } from "@/generated/routes";

    export default function CreateUser() {
      const form = useForm({
        name: "",
        email: "",
      });

      function handleSubmit(e: FormEvent) {
        e.preventDefault();
        form.post(route("users.store"));
      }

      return (
        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
          <input
            value={form.data.name}
            onChange={(e) => form.setData("name", e.target.value)}
          />
          {form.errors.name && <p className="error">{form.errors.name}</p>}

          <input
            type="email"
            value={form.data.email}
            onChange={(e) => form.setData("email", e.target.value)}
          />
          {form.errors.email && <p className="error">{form.errors.email}</p>}

          <button type="submit" disabled={form.processing}>
            Create User
          </button>
        </form>
      );
    }
    ```

=== "Vue 3"

    ```vue title="resources/pages/Users/Create.vue"
    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { useForm } from "@inertiajs/vue3";
    import { route } from "@/generated/routes";

    const form = useForm({
      name: "",
      email: "",
    });

    function submit() {
      form.post(route("users.store"));
    }
    </script>

    <template>
      <form @submit.prevent="submit">
        <input v-model="form.name" />
        <p v-if="form.errors.name">{{ form.errors.name }}</p>

        <input v-model="form.email" type="email" />
        <p v-if="form.errors.email">{{ form.errors.email }}</p>

        <button type="submit" :disabled="form.processing">Create User</button>
      </form>
    </template>
    ```

=== "Svelte 5"

    <!-- docs-example: skip -->
    ```svelte title="resources/pages/Users/Create.svelte"
    <script lang="ts">
      import { useForm } from "@inertiajs/svelte";
      import { route } from "@/generated/routes";

      const form = useForm({
        name: "",
        email: "",
      });

      function submit(e: SubmitEvent) {
        e.preventDefault();
        $form.post(route("users.store"));
      }
    </script>

    <form onsubmit={submit}>
      <input bind:value={$form.name} />
      {#if $form.errors.name}<p>{$form.errors.name}</p>{/if}

      <input type="email" bind:value={$form.email} />
      {#if $form.errors.email}<p>{$form.errors.email}</p>{/if}

      <button type="submit" disabled={$form.processing}>Create User</button>
    </form>
    ```

---

## Server-Side Validation & `error`

Litestar Vite supports both **automatic schema validation** (from `msgspec.Struct`, Pydantic, or Litestar DTO constraints) and **manual domain errors** via [`error(connection, key, message)`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.error):

```python
from typing import Annotated, Any
from litestar import Request, post
from msgspec import Meta, Struct
from litestar_vite.inertia import InertiaBack, InertiaRedirect, error, flash


class CreateUserPayload(Struct):
    name: Annotated[str, Meta(min_length=2)]
    email: Annotated[str, Meta(pattern=r"^[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+$")]


@post("/users", name="users.store", sync_to_thread=False)
def create_user(
    request: Request[Any, Any, Any],
    data: CreateUserPayload,
) -> InertiaRedirect | InertiaBack:
    """Validate payload and check domain uniqueness."""
    if data.email == "taken@example.com":
        error(request, "email", "That email address is already registered.")
        return InertiaBack(request)

    flash(request, f"Created {data.name}", category="success")
    return InertiaRedirect(request, redirect_to="/users")
```

### Error Bags

When a page contains multiple forms sharing field names (such as `email`), pass `{ errorBag: "inviteUser" }` in `form.post(url, { errorBag: "inviteUser" })`. The Inertia client sends the `X-Inertia-Error-Bag: inviteUser` request header, and `InertiaMiddleware` automatically scopes any `error(request, "email", ...)` or validation errors under `props.errors.inviteUser`.

### Custom Error Pages

Configure `InertiaConfig(redirect_404="/404", redirect_unauthorized_to="/login")` for automatic redirects, or register a custom Litestar `exception_handlers` mapping returning `InertiaResponse(..., status_code=exc.status_code)` with `component="Error"` to render a branded Inertia error page while preserving the HTTP status code.

---

## Live Validation with Laravel Precognition

[Laravel Precognition](https://laravel.com/docs/precognition) lets your frontend validate form fields against your exact Litestar validation rules as the user types, **without executing the route handler body**:

1. Enable `InertiaConfig(precognition=True)` in `ViteConfig`.
2. Decorate your mutation route handler with [`@precognition`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.precognition.precognition):

```python
from typing import Annotated
from litestar import post
from msgspec import Meta, Struct
from litestar_vite.inertia import precognition


class CreateWorkspaceInput(Struct):
    name: Annotated[str, Meta(min_length=3, max_length=60)]
    slug: Annotated[str, Meta(pattern=r"^[a-z0-9-]+$")]


@post("/workspaces", name="workspaces.store", sync_to_thread=False)
@precognition
def create_workspace(data: CreateWorkspaceInput) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Only runs on real form submission; Precognition requests short-circuit with 204."""
    return {"slug": data.slug}
```

### How Precognition Works

- When the client sends `Precognition: true` (and optional `Precognition-Validate-Only: slug`), Litestar validates `data: CreateWorkspaceInput` first (you can also inspect `request.is_precognition` and `request.precognition_validate_only` inside custom guards or dependencies).
- If validation fails, Litestar returns 422 Unprocessable Entity with `{ "message": "...", "errors": { "slug": ["..."] } }` filtered to `Precognition-Validate-Only`.
- If validation passes on a `Precognition: true` request, `@precognition` short-circuits before executing `create_workspace` and returns 204 No Content with `Precognition: true` and `Precognition-Success: true`.
- `litestar-vite-plugin/inertia-helpers` also exports `isPrecognitionSuccess`, `isPrecognitionError`, `extractPrecognitionErrors`, and `PrecognitionHeaders` for custom client integrations.

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/index.md -->

# Inertia.js Overview & Protocol Lifecycle

[Inertia.js](https://inertiajs.com) lets you build modern React, Vue 3, and Svelte 5 single-page applications using classic server-side routing and controllers. Instead of building a separate REST or GraphQL API for every screen, your Litestar route handlers declare `component="Users/Index"` and return Python `dict`, `msgspec.Struct`, `dataclass`, or Pydantic models directly.

[Interactive Architecture Diagram: diagram-inertia-lifecycle.html]
---

## How the Inertia Protocol Works in Litestar

1. **Initial Full-Page Visit**:
   - The browser sends a standard HTTP request without an `X-Inertia` header.
   - `InertiaResponse` serializes the `PageProps` JSON envelope into `<script type="application/json" id="app_page" data-page="app">` (or the legacy `data-page` attribute on `#app` when `use_script_element=False`).
   - When `InertiaConfig(ssr=True)` is enabled, Litestar Vite pre-renders the initial HTML via the SSR IPC transport before returning the page.
2. **Subsequent Client Navigation**:
   - Clicking an Inertia `<Link>` or calling `router.visit()` sends an XHR/Fetch request with `X-Inertia: true` and `X-Inertia-Version`.
   - Litestar detects the Inertia visit and returns `application/json` containing only the `PageProps` envelope, swapping the page component in place without a full browser reload.
3. **Deferred Props & Partial Reloads**:
   - Props wrapped in `defer()` are omitted from the initial response and listed in `deferredProps`.
   - Immediately after mounting the initial page, the Inertia client fires batched background partial reloads to resolve each deferred group.
4. **Mutations & Asset Version Rotation**:
   - Following POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE requests, `InertiaMiddleware` converts 302 redirects into 303 See Other so the browser follows up with a GET request.
   - If the frontend bundle hash changes between deployments (`X-Inertia-Version` mismatch), Litestar responds with 409 Conflict and `X-Inertia-Location`, prompting a clean full-page reload.

---

## Protocol Headers & Status Codes

| Header | Direction | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Inertia` | Request & Response | `"true"` marks an Inertia XHR/Fetch navigation and JSON `PageProps` response. |
| `X-Inertia-Version` | Request | Current asset manifest hash known by the client; triggers 409 Conflict on mismatch. |
| `X-Inertia-Location` | Response (409) | Target URL for forced full-page reload or external redirect (`InertiaExternalRedirect`). |
| `X-Inertia-Partial-Component` | Request | Component name targeted by a partial reload (`only` / `except`). |
| `X-Inertia-Partial-Data` | Request | Comma-separated list of prop keys to include during a partial reload. |
| `X-Inertia-Partial-Except` | Request | Comma-separated list of prop keys to exclude during a partial reload. |
| `X-Inertia-Reset` | Request | Comma-separated list of merged prop keys to reset before evaluating new values. |
| `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props` | Request | Comma-separated list of `once()` prop keys already cached on the client. |
| `X-Inertia-Error-Bag` | Request | Optional error bag namespace for scoping form validation errors. |
| `Precognition` | Request & Response | `"true"` activates live Laravel Precognition validation without side effects. |
| `Precognition-Validate-Only` | Request | Comma-separated field names to filter validation errors during live typing. |
| `Precognition-Success` | Response (204) | `"true"` confirms live validation succeeded. |

| HTTP Status | Meaning in Inertia |
| --- | --- |
| 200 OK | Full HTML shell on initial visit, or JSON `PageProps` envelope when `X-Inertia: true`. |
| 204 No Content | Successful `@precognition` live validation check (`Precognition-Success: true`). |
| 303 See Other | Redirect following `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE` so the browser follows with `GET`. |
| 409 Conflict | Asset version mismatch or `InertiaExternalRedirect` (`X-Inertia-Location` header). |
| 422 Unprocessable Entity | Precognition live validation error payload (`{ message, errors }`). |

---

## The PageProps Wire Envelope

Optional protocol keys (`flash`, `deferredProps`, `mergeProps`, `prependProps`, `deepMergeProps`, `matchPropsOn`, `scrollProps`, `onceProps`) are **omitted** when empty to keep wire payloads minimal:

```json
{
  "component": "Posts/Index",
  "props": {
    "errors": {},
    "csrf_token": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015",
    "auth": { "user": { "id": 1, "name": "Alice" } },
    "posts": [{ "id": 10, "title": "Hello Inertia" }]
  },
  "url": "/posts?page=1",
  "version": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924",
  "encryptHistory": false,
  "clearHistory": false,
  "flash": { "success": ["Post published"] },
  "deferredProps": { "default": ["analytics"] },
  "mergeProps": ["posts"],
  "matchPropsOn": ["posts.id"]
}
```

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/merging-and-infinite-scroll.md -->

# Merging Props & Infinite Scroll

By default, partial reloads replace existing prop values. Using [`merge()`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.merge), [`scroll_props()`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.scroll_props), or `@get(..., infinite_scroll=True)` instructs the Inertia client to **append, prepend, or deep-merge** incoming items into existing client arrays.

---

## Prop Merge Strategies (`merge`)

```python
from litestar import get
from litestar_vite.inertia import merge


@get("/notifications", component="Notifications/Index", sync_to_thread=False)
def list_notifications(page: int = 1) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Demonstrate append, prepend, and deduplicated merge strategies."""
    items = [{"id": page * 10 + 1, "text": f"Notification #{page}"}]
    return {
        # Append new items and deduplicate by 'id'
        "notifications": merge("notifications", items, strategy="append", match_on="id"),
        # Prepend newest activity items at the top of the list
        "live_activity": merge("live_activity", items, strategy="prepend", match_on="id"),
        # Deep-merge nested filter counters
        "facets": merge("facets", {"unread": 3}, strategy="deep"),
    }
```

| Parameter | Options | Wire Protocol Field | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strategy="append"` | Default | `mergeProps: ["notifications"]` | Appends new array items to the end of the existing client array. |
| `strategy="prepend"` | `"prepend"` | `prependProps: ["live_activity"]` | Prepends new array items to the start of the existing client array. |
| `strategy="deep"` | `"deep"` | `deepMergeProps: ["facets"]` | Recursively merges nested objects and arrays. |
| `match_on` | <code>str &#124; list[str]</code> | `matchPropsOn: ["notifications.id"]` | Deduplicates merged items by matching one or more keys (updating existing items in place). |

!!! tip
    To discard merged items and start fresh (for example, when the user changes a search filter), pass `reset: ["notifications"]` in `router.visit(url, { only: ["notifications"], reset: ["notifications"] })`.

---

## Automatic Infinite Scroll

When your route handler returns a Litestar `OffsetPagination[T]`, `ClassicPagination[T]`, or `advanced_alchemy` pagination container, setting `infinite_scroll=True` in the route decorator automatically configures `mergeProps` and `scrollProps` (`pageName`, `currentPage`, `previousPage`, `nextPage`):

```python
from litestar import get
from litestar.pagination import ClassicPagination
from msgspec import Struct


class FeedPost(Struct):
    id: int
    title: str


@get("/feed", component="Feed/Index", key="posts", infinite_scroll=True, sync_to_thread=False)
def feed_index(page: int = 1, page_size: int = 20) -> ClassicPagination[FeedPost]:
    """Automatically configures mergeProps=['posts'] and scrollProps metadata."""
    posts = [FeedPost(id=page * 100 + i, title=f"Post {i}") for i in range(1, 4)]
    return ClassicPagination(
        items=posts,
        page_size=page_size,
        current_page=page,
        total_pages=5,
    )
```

### Manual `scroll_props` Configuration

If you build custom cursor or keyset pagination without `ClassicPagination` / `OffsetPagination`, attach [`scroll_props()`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.scroll_props) explicitly:

```python
from litestar import get
from litestar_vite.inertia import InertiaResponse, merge, scroll_props


@get("/timeline", component="Timeline/Index", sync_to_thread=False)
def timeline(page: int = 1) -> InertiaResponse[dict[str, object]]:
    """Configure custom pagination metadata with scroll_props()."""
    items = [{"id": page, "body": f"Entry {page}"}]
    return InertiaResponse(
        {"entries": merge("entries", items, match_on="id")},
        scroll_props=scroll_props(
            page_name="page",
            current_page=page,
            previous_page=page - 1 if page > 1 else None,
            next_page=page + 1 if page < 10 else None,
        ),
    )
```

---

## Frontend Infinite Scroll

Pair `merge()` and `scrollProps` with `<WhenVisible always>` at the bottom of your list. When `infinite_scroll=True` or `scroll_props()` is used, Inertia attaches pagination metadata on `page.props.scrollProps` (with `nextPage`, `previousPage`, `currentPage`, and `pageName`):

=== "React"

    ```tsx title="resources/pages/Feed/Index.tsx"
    import { usePage, WhenVisible } from "@inertiajs/react";

    interface FeedProps {
      posts: Array<{ id: number; title: string }>;
      scrollProps?: {
        nextPage?: number | null;
      };
    }

    export default function FeedIndex({ posts }: FeedProps) {
      const { props } = usePage<{ scrollProps?: { nextPage?: number | null } }>();
      const nextPage = props.scrollProps?.nextPage;

      return (
        <div>
          <ul>
            {posts.map((post) => (
              <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
            ))}
          </ul>

          {nextPage && (
            <WhenVisible
              always
              params={{
                data: { page: nextPage },
                only: ["posts"],
                preserveUrl: true,
              }}
              fallback={<div>Loading more posts...</div>}
            >
              <div />
            </WhenVisible>
          )}
        </div>
      );
    }
    ```

=== "Vue 3"

    ```vue title="resources/pages/Feed/Index.vue"
    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { computed } from "vue";
    import { usePage, WhenVisible } from "@inertiajs/vue3";

    defineProps<{
      posts: Array<{ id: number; title: string }>;
    }>();

    const page = usePage<{ scrollProps?: { nextPage?: number | null } }>();
    const nextPage = computed(() => page.props.scrollProps?.nextPage);
    </script>

    <template>
      <ul>
        <li v-for="post in posts" :key="post.id">{{ post.title }}</li>
      </ul>

      <WhenVisible
        v-if="nextPage"
        always
        :params="{
          data: { page: nextPage },
          only: ['posts'],
          preserveUrl: true,
        }"
      >
        <template #fallback>
          <div>Loading more posts...</div>
        </template>
        <div />
      </WhenVisible>
    </template>
    ```

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/pages-and-responses.md -->

# Pages & Responses

In `mode="hybrid"`, any Litestar route handler can render an Inertia page component by setting `component="..."` (or `page="..."`) in the route decorator and returning a dictionary or typed model.

---

## Declaring Page Handlers

You can return a plain `dict[str, Any]` or `msgspec.Struct` when `component="..."` is declared on the route decorator, or return an explicit [`InertiaResponse`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.InertiaResponse) when you need per-response flags such as `encrypt_history=True`, `clear_history=True`, `template_name`, or `prop_filter`:

```python title="docs/examples/inertia/pages_and_responses.py"
"""Inertia.js v2 page components, InertiaResponse, and redirects."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from litestar import Litestar, Request, get, post
from msgspec import Struct

from litestar_vite import InertiaConfig, RuntimeConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin
from litestar_vite.inertia import InertiaExternalRedirect, InertiaRedirect, InertiaResponse


class InvoiceSummary(Struct, frozen=True, gc=False):
    """Typed invoice item serialized into Inertia PageProps."""

    id: int
    customer: str
    total_cents: int


@get("/invoices", component="Invoices/Index", sync_to_thread=False)
def list_invoices() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return Inertia page props via the ``component=`` route option."""
    return {
        "invoices": [
            InvoiceSummary(id=101, customer="Acme Corp", total_cents=12500),
            InvoiceSummary(id=102, customer="Globex", total_cents=8400),
        ]
    }


@get("/invoices/featured", component="Invoices/Show", sync_to_thread=False)
def show_featured_invoice() -> InertiaResponse[InvoiceSummary]:
    """Return an explicit ``InertiaResponse`` with history encryption enabled."""
    return InertiaResponse(InvoiceSummary(id=101, customer="Acme Corp", total_cents=12500), encrypt_history=True)


@post("/invoices/checkout", sync_to_thread=False)
def start_external_checkout(request: Request[Any, Any, Any]) -> InertiaExternalRedirect:
    """Trigger an external ``409 Conflict`` + ``X-Inertia-Location`` redirect."""
    return InertiaExternalRedirect(request, redirect_to="https://billing.example.com/checkout")


def create_app() -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar app with Inertia v2 page and redirect handlers."""
    vite_config = ViteConfig(
        mode="hybrid",
        dev_mode=True,
        inertia=InertiaConfig(root_template="index.html"),
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(start_dev_server=False),
    )
    return Litestar(
        route_handlers=[list_invoices, show_featured_invoice, start_external_checkout],
        plugins=[VitePlugin(config=vite_config)],
    )


def main() -> None:
    """Verify Inertia page responses and redirect primitives."""
    app = create_app()
    assert app is not None
    response = InertiaResponse(InvoiceSummary(id=101, customer="Acme Corp", total_cents=12500), encrypt_history=True)
    assert response.encrypt_history is True
    assert InertiaRedirect is not None


__all__ = ("InvoiceSummary", "create_app", "list_invoices", "main", "show_featured_invoice", "start_external_checkout")
```

### Nested Page Components

Organize page components into subdirectories (`resources/pages/Users/Index.tsx`, `resources/pages/Settings/Profile.tsx`) and reference them with forward-slash paths (`component="Users/Index"`). `resolvePageComponent` maps the component string directly to `./pages/${name}.tsx` (or `.vue` / `.svelte`).

---

## Direct Model Returns

When a route handler returns a `msgspec.Struct`, `dataclass`, or Pydantic `BaseModel` directly instead of a `dict`, `InertiaResponse` serializes its top-level fields as the page's props — respecting `msgspec.Struct(rename="camel")` and `msgspec.field(name=...)` aliases automatically:

```python
from litestar import get
from msgspec import Struct


class UserProfileProps(Struct, rename="camel"):
    user_id: int
    display_name: str
    is_verified: bool


@get("/profile", component="Profile/Show", sync_to_thread=False)
def show_profile() -> UserProfileProps:
    """Serializes as { userId: 42, displayName: 'Ada', isVerified: true }."""
    return UserProfileProps(user_id=42, display_name="Ada", is_verified=True)
```

---

## Consuming Page Props on the Frontend

=== "React"

    ```tsx title="resources/pages/Profile/Show.tsx"
    import { Head } from "@inertiajs/react";

    interface ProfileShowProps {
      userId: number;
      displayName: string;
      isVerified: boolean;
    }

    export default function ProfileShow({ displayName, isVerified }: ProfileShowProps) {
      return (
        <>
          <Head title={`${displayName} — Profile`} />
          <h1>{displayName}</h1>
          {isVerified && <span>Verified</span>}
        </>
      );
    }
    ```

=== "Vue 3"

    ```vue title="resources/pages/Profile/Show.vue"
    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { Head } from "@inertiajs/vue3";

    defineProps<{
      userId: number;
      displayName: string;
      isVerified: boolean;
    }>();
    </script>

    <template>
      <Head :title="`${displayName} — Profile`" />
      <h1>{{ displayName }}</h1>
      <span v-if="isVerified">Verified</span>
    </template>
    ```

=== "Svelte 5"

    ```svelte title="resources/pages/Profile/Show.svelte"
    <script lang="ts">
      interface Props {
        userId: number;
        displayName: string;
        isVerified: boolean;
      }

      let { displayName, isVerified }: Props = $props();
    </script>

    <svelte:head>
      <title>{displayName} — Profile</title>
    </svelte:head>

    <h1>{displayName}</h1>
    {#if isVerified}
      <span>Verified</span>
    {/if}
    ```

---

## Automatic Pagination Container Unwrapping

When a route handler returns a Litestar `OffsetPagination[T]`, `ClassicPagination[T]`, or `advanced_alchemy` pagination container, `InertiaResponse` automatically extracts the items into the prop key specified by `key="..."` (default `"items"`) alongside pagination metadata (`total`, `limit`, `offset`, or `current_page`, `total_pages`):

```python
from litestar import get
from litestar.pagination import OffsetPagination
from msgspec import Struct


class PostSummary(Struct):
    id: int
    title: str


@get("/posts", component="Posts/Index", key="posts", sync_to_thread=False)
def list_posts(limit: int = 10, offset: int = 0) -> OffsetPagination[PostSummary]:
    """Unwraps items into props['posts'] with pagination metadata."""
    items = [PostSummary(id=1, title="Hello Litestar")]
    return OffsetPagination(items=items, limit=limit, offset=offset, total=1)
```

---

## Server-Side Prop Filtering (`only` and `except_`)

Use [`only(*keys)`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.only) or [`except_(*keys)`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.except_) with `InertiaResponse(..., prop_filter=...)` to restrict which keys from a shared service dictionary or model are serialized into `props`:

```python
from typing import Any
from litestar import Request, get
from litestar_vite.inertia import InertiaResponse, except_


@get("/users/{user_id:int}", component="Users/Show", sync_to_thread=False)
def show_user(request: Request[Any, Any, Any], user_id: int) -> InertiaResponse[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Exclude internal audit fields on the server before serialization."""
    record = {"id": user_id, "name": "Alice", "password_hash": "...", "internal_notes": "..."}
    return InertiaResponse(
        record,
        prop_filter=except_("password_hash", "internal_notes"),
    )
```

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/partial-reloads-and-deferred.md -->

# Partial Reloads & Deferred Props

Inertia gives you fine-grained control over **when** each prop is evaluated on the server. Choosing the right prop wrapper keeps initial page loads instantaneous while avoiding manual `fetch()` state management.

---

## Prop Evaluation Matrix

| Helper | Initial Load | Partial Reload | Client Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Plain value** | Included | Included unless filtered | Replaces prop value |
| [`always`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.always) | Always included | Always included (bypasses `only` / `except_`) | Replaces prop value on every visit (auth, errors) |
| [`defer`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.defer) | Queued in `deferredProps` | Auto-fetched by `<Deferred>` after mount | Loaded in grouped background requests after initial paint |
| [`once`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.once) | Included | Skipped once cached (`only` forces refresh) | Cached across client page navigations (`onceProps`) |
| [`optional`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.optional) | Excluded | Only when listed in `only` | Designed for `<WhenVisible>` viewport loading |
| [`lazy`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.lazy) | Excluded | Only when listed in `only` | Classic on-demand partial reload prop |
| [`merge`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.merge) | Included | Appends, prepends, or deep-merges | Combines items in place during partial reloads (`mergeProps`) |

---

## Complete Server Example

```python title="docs/examples/inertia/props_and_reloads.py"
"""Inertia.js v2 deferred props, partial reloads, once caching, and infinite scroll."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from litestar import Litestar, get

from litestar_vite import InertiaConfig, RuntimeConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin
from litestar_vite.inertia import always, defer, lazy, merge, once, optional, scroll_props


def _load_slow_analytics() -> dict[str, int]:
    """Simulate an expensive analytics query deferred until after initial render."""
    return {"weeklyActive": 1420, "conversionRateBps": 385}


def _load_audit_log() -> list[str]:
    """Simulate an on-demand audit trail loaded only when requested."""
    return ["user.login", "invoice.exported"]


@get("/analytics", component="Analytics/Dashboard", sync_to_thread=False)
def analytics_dashboard() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Combine eager, deferred, once-cached, optional, and merged props."""
    return {
        "permissions": always("permissions", {"canExport": True}),
        "summary": {"totalRevenue": 94200},
        "metrics": defer("metrics", _load_slow_analytics, group="charts"),
        "featureCatalog": once("featureCatalog", lambda: ["sso", "audit_stream"]),
        "auditLog": optional("auditLog", _load_audit_log),
        "legacySummary": lazy("legacySummary", lambda: {"archived": 12}),
        "events": merge(
            "events",
            [{"id": 1, "title": "Deployment succeeded"}, {"id": 2, "title": "Backup completed"}],
            strategy="append",
            match_on="id",
        ),
        "scroll": scroll_props(page_name="page", current_page=1, next_page=2),
    }


def create_app() -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar app demonstrating Inertia v2 prop wrappers."""
    vite_config = ViteConfig(
        mode="hybrid",
        dev_mode=True,
        inertia=InertiaConfig(root_template="index.html"),
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(start_dev_server=False),
    )
    return Litestar(route_handlers=[analytics_dashboard], plugins=[VitePlugin(config=vite_config)])


def main() -> None:
    """Verify Inertia v2 prop wrapper construction."""
    app = create_app()
    assert app is not None
    deferred = defer("metrics", _load_slow_analytics, group="charts")
    merged = merge("events", [{"id": 1}], strategy="append", match_on="id")
    assert deferred.group == "charts"
    assert merged.strategy == "append"
    assert merged.match_on == ["id"]


__all__ = ("analytics_dashboard", "create_app", "main")
```

!!! important
    **Avoid the False-Lazy Pitfall**: Always pass a callable reference (`defer("metrics", _load_slow_analytics)` or `lazy("report", lambda: build_report(org_id))`) rather than calling the function eagerly (`defer("metrics", _load_slow_analytics())`). Both synchronous and `async def` callables are supported; async callables are resolved concurrently on the event loop by `InertiaResponse`.

---

## Client-Initiated Partial Reloads

Use `router.reload({ only: [...] })` or `router.reload({ except: [...] })` to refresh a subset of props on the current page without re-evaluating unrelated database queries:

```typescript
import { router } from "@inertiajs/react";

// Refresh only the "metrics" and "notifications" props
router.reload({ only: ["metrics", "notifications"] });

// Refresh everything except the heavy "catalog" prop
router.reload({ except: ["catalog"] });

// Reset merged arrays before reloading
router.reload({ only: ["feed"], reset: ["feed"] });
```

---

## Deferred Props & Grouped Resolution

Props wrapped in `defer(key, fn, group="default")` are omitted from the initial response and grouped in `deferredProps: { default: ["metrics"], charts: ["revenue", "retention"] }`. Props in the same `group` are fetched together in a single background request after the page mounts:

=== "React"

    ```tsx title="resources/pages/Analytics/Dashboard.tsx"
    import { Deferred, WhenVisible } from "@inertiajs/react";

    export default function AnalyticsDashboard() {
      return (
        <div>
          <Deferred data="metrics" fallback={<div>Loading metrics...</div>}>
            <MetricsChart />
          </Deferred>

          <WhenVisible data="audit_log" buffer={200} fallback={<div>Scrolling into view...</div>}>
            <AuditLogTable />
          </WhenVisible>
        </div>
      );
    }
    ```

=== "Vue 3"

    ```vue title="resources/pages/Analytics/Dashboard.vue"
    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { Deferred, WhenVisible } from "@inertiajs/vue3";
    </script>

    <template>
      <Deferred data="metrics">
        <template #fallback>
          <div>Loading metrics...</div>
        </template>
        <MetricsChart />
      </Deferred>

      <WhenVisible data="audit_log" :buffer="200">
        <template #fallback>
          <div>Scrolling into view...</div>
        </template>
        <AuditLogTable />
      </WhenVisible>
    </template>
    ```

---

## Viewport-Triggered Loading (`optional` + `<WhenVisible>`)

Wrap below-the-fold data in `optional("audit_log", load_audit_log)` on the server and `<WhenVisible data="audit_log" buffer={200}>` on the client. An `IntersectionObserver` triggers a partial reload (`only: ["audit_log"]`) when the element approaches within 200px of the viewport. Pass `always` (`<WhenVisible data="audit_log" always>`) to re-fetch every time the element enters the viewport.

---

## Client-Cached Props (`once`) & Fluent Chaining

- **`once("countries", load_countries)`**: Evaluated on the first visit and advertised in `onceProps: {"countries": {"prop": "countries"}}`. On subsequent Inertia navigations, the client sends `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props: countries` so the server skips re-evaluating `load_countries`. Explicitly requesting `only: ["countries"]` forces a refresh.
- **`defer("catalog", load_catalog).once()`**: Defers the expensive query until after initial paint, then caches the resolved value in `onceProps` across subsequent page navigations.

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/routing-and-links.md -->

# Routing, Links & Redirects

In Inertia applications, **all routing is defined on the server** using standard Litestar `@get`, `@post`, `@put`, `@patch`, and `@delete` decorators. You do not need `react-router` or `vue-router`.

---

## How Litestar Routing Compares to Laravel + Ziggy

| Concept | Laravel + Ziggy | Litestar + Litestar Vite |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Route Declaration** | `Route::get('/users/{id}', ...)->name('users.show')` | `@get("/users/{user_id:int}", name="users.show", component="Users/Show")` |
| **Frontend URL Helper** | Ziggy `route('users.show', { id: 1 })` | Native generated `route("users.show", { user_id: 1 })` in `routes.ts` |
| **Parameter Type Safety** | Runtime lookup | **Compile-time TypeScript check** (autocomplete on route names & required path/query params) |
| **Plain URL Strings** | `<Link href="/users/1">` | `<Link href="/users/1">` (first-class citizen) |

---

## Client-Side Navigation with `<Link>` and `route`

Use Inertia's `<Link>` component for internal navigation so clicks are intercepted as lightweight XHR/Fetch requests instead of full browser reloads. Pair `<Link>` with the generated `route()` function from `@/generated/routes` for compile-time URL safety:

=== "React"

    ```tsx title="resources/components/Nav.tsx"
    import { Link } from "@inertiajs/react";
    import { route } from "@/generated/routes";

    export function Nav({ userId }: { userId: number }) {
      return (
        <nav>
          <Link href={route("dashboard")}>Dashboard</Link>
          <Link href={route("users.show", { user_id: userId })}>My Profile</Link>
          <Link href={route("logout")} method="post" as="button">
            Sign Out
          </Link>
        </nav>
      );
    }
    ```

=== "Vue 3"

    ```vue title="resources/components/Nav.vue"
    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { Link } from "@inertiajs/vue3";
    import { route } from "@/generated/routes";

    defineProps<{ userId: number }>();
    </script>

    <template>
      <nav>
        <Link :href="route('dashboard')">Dashboard</Link>
        <Link :href="route('users.show', { user_id: userId })">My Profile</Link>
        <Link :href="route('logout')" method="post" as="button">Sign Out</Link>
      </nav>
    </template>
    ```

=== "Svelte 5"

    ```svelte title="resources/components/Nav.svelte"
    <script lang="ts">
      import { router } from "@inertiajs/svelte";
      import { route } from "@/generated/routes";

      let { userId }: { userId: number } = $props();
    </script>

    <nav>
      <a href={route("dashboard")} onclick={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); router.visit(route("dashboard")); }}>
        Dashboard
      </a>
      <button type="button" onclick={() => router.post(route("logout"))}>
        Sign Out
      </button>
    </nav>
    ```

### Global Route Helper

If you want `route()` available globally without importing it in every file (similar to Laravel Ziggy), set `TypeGenConfig(global_route=True)` in Python and register `window.route = route` in your application entrypoint.

---

## Redirect Primitives

Inertia expects specific HTTP status codes when redirecting after form submissions or navigating to external domains:

| Class | Status / Header | Security & Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`InertiaRedirect(request, redirect_to="/...")`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.InertiaRedirect) | 303 See Other (after `PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`) or 302 Found | Validates that `redirect_to` is same-origin (or relative) to prevent open-redirect vulnerabilities, and preserves staged `flash()` / `error()` session data. |
| [`InertiaBack(request)`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.InertiaBack) | 303 See Other to `Referer` | Redirects back to the referring page if the `Referer` header matches the request's origin; falls back to `base_url` otherwise. |
| [`InertiaExternalRedirect(request, redirect_to="https://...")`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.InertiaExternalRedirect) | 409 Conflict + `X-Inertia-Location` | Instructs the Inertia client to perform a full `window.location` redirect to an external URL (e.g., Stripe Checkout or an OAuth provider). |

---

## The POST-Redirect-GET Pattern

Following any mutation (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`), return an `InertiaRedirect` or `InertiaBack` so the browser follows up with a `GET` visit and updates the page props cleanly:

```python
from typing import Any
from litestar import Request, post
from litestar_vite.inertia import InertiaBack, InertiaExternalRedirect, InertiaRedirect, flash


@post("/projects/{project_id:int}/archive", sync_to_thread=False)
def archive_project(request: Request[Any, Any, Any], project_id: int) -> InertiaRedirect:
    """Archive a project, flash a notification, and redirect to the index."""
    flash(request, f"Project #{project_id} archived.", category="success")
    return InertiaRedirect(request, redirect_to="/projects")


@post("/comments", sync_to_thread=False)
def post_comment(request: Request[Any, Any, Any]) -> InertiaBack:
    """Return to whichever page submitted the comment."""
    flash(request, "Comment added.", category="info")
    return InertiaBack(request)


@post("/billing/checkout", sync_to_thread=False)
def start_checkout(request: Request[Any, Any, Any]) -> InertiaExternalRedirect:
    """Redirect outside the SPA to an external payment gateway."""
    return InertiaExternalRedirect(request, redirect_to="https://checkout.stripe.com/pay/cs_test_123")
```

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/security-and-versioning.md -->

# Security, History Encryption & Asset Versioning

This guide covers CSRF protection with `cookie_httponly=True`, encrypting sensitive `window.history.state` payloads, and zero-downtime asset versioning across rolling deployments.

---

## CSRF Protection

Litestar's `CSRFConfig` protects state-changing requests (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`). Litestar Vite supports `CSRFConfig(cookie_httponly=True)` out of the box by injecting the CSRF token into `props.csrf_token` (in Inertia mode) and `window.__LITESTAR_CSRF__` (in SPA mode) so JavaScript never needs to read `document.cookie`:

```python title="app.py"
from litestar import Litestar
from litestar.config.csrf import CSRFConfig
from litestar_vite import InertiaConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin

app = Litestar(
    route_handlers=[],
    csrf_config=CSRFConfig(
        secret="replace-with-32-byte-production-secret",
        cookie_httponly=True,
        header_name="x-csrf-token",
    ),
    plugins=[
        VitePlugin(config=ViteConfig(mode="hybrid", inertia=InertiaConfig())),
    ],
)
```

### Automatic CSRF Header Injection

Import `csrfHeaders`, `getCsrfToken`, or `csrfFetch` from `litestar-vite-plugin/helpers` and configure Inertia's `visitOptions` so every non-GET visit includes the `X-CSRF-Token` header automatically:

```typescript title="resources/main.ts"
import { csrfHeaders, csrfFetch, getCsrfToken } from "litestar-vite-plugin/helpers";

// 1. Inside createInertiaApp({ defaults: { ... } }):
const defaults = {
  visitOptions: (_href: string, options: { headers?: Record<string, string> }) => ({
    headers: csrfHeaders(options.headers ?? {}),
  }),
};

// 2. For standalone fetch() requests outside Inertia:
async function pingAction() {
  const token = getCsrfToken();
  return csrfFetch("/api/ping", { method: "POST", headers: { "X-Requested-With": token } });
}
```

### Token Resolution Order

`getCsrfToken()` resolves the active token deterministically in this order:

1. `window.__LITESTAR_CSRF__` (injected by the SPA HTML transformer)
2. `<meta name="csrf-token" content="...">` (used in Jinja2 / HTMX templates)
3. `<script type="application/json" id="app_page" data-page="app">` (`props.csrf_token`)
4. `<div id="app" data-page="...">` (`props.csrf_token`)

---

## History Encryption

By default, Inertia caches each visited page's `PageProps` inside the browser's `window.history.state` so pressing the **Back** button restores the page instantaneously. If your application displays sensitive data (financial records, PII, medical charts) on shared computers, enable **History Encryption** so cached state is encrypted with AES-GCM via the browser's Web Crypto API and wiped upon logout:

```python
from typing import Any
from litestar import Request, get, post
from litestar_vite.inertia import InertiaRedirect, InertiaResponse, clear_history


@get("/billing/statements", component="Billing/Statements", sync_to_thread=False)
def view_statements() -> InertiaResponse[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Encrypt history state for this specific sensitive route."""
    return InertiaResponse(
        {"statements": [{"id": 1, "amount": "$420.00"}]},
        encrypt_history=True,
    )


@post("/logout", name="logout", sync_to_thread=False)
def logout_user(request: Request[Any, Any, Any]) -> InertiaRedirect:
    """Clear user session and rotate browser history encryption keys."""
    request.session.clear()
    clear_history(request)
    return InertiaRedirect(request, redirect_to="/login")
```

- **Global Encryption**: Set `InertiaConfig(encrypt_history=True)` to encrypt history state across all Inertia responses.
- **HTTPS / Secure Context Requirement**: History encryption uses `window.crypto.subtle`, which requires either `https://` in production or `http://localhost` / `http://127.0.0.1` in development.

---

## Asset Versioning & Rolling Deployments

In a single-page app, users can keep a browser tab open for hours or days. When you deploy a new frontend bundle:

1. `ViteAssetLoader.version_id` computes a deterministic SHA-256 digest of your `manifest.json` (in production) or `"1.0"` (in development).
2. Every Inertia visit sends `X-Inertia-Version: <version_id>`.
3. If a `GET` request arrives with an outdated `X-Inertia-Version`, `InertiaMiddleware` responds with 409 Conflict and `X-Inertia-Location: <request.url>`.
4. The Inertia client intercepts the 409 response and transparently performs a full `window.location` reload so the browser downloads the newly deployed JS/CSS bundles.

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/shared-data-and-flash.md -->

# Shared Data & Flash Messages

Cross-cutting concerns like the currently authenticated user, organization permissions, and toast notifications (`flash`) are shared across pages without repeating props in every route handler.

---

## Per-Request Shared Props (`share`)

Call [`share(connection, key, value)`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.share) inside route handlers, guards, dependencies, or middleware to attach props to the current request's Inertia envelope:

```python title="docs/examples/inertia/shared_and_flash.py"
"""Inertia.js v2 shared session props, flash messages, validation errors, and Precognition."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Annotated, Any

from litestar import Litestar, Request, post
from litestar.params import Body
from msgspec import Struct

from litestar_vite import InertiaConfig, RuntimeConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin
from litestar_vite.inertia import error, flash, precognition, share


class AuthenticatedUser(Struct, frozen=True, gc=False):
    """Typed current user model registered in ``shared_page_prop_types``."""

    id: int
    email: str
    role: str


class CreateProjectPayload(Struct, frozen=True, gc=False):
    """Form payload validated by both live Precognition and final submission."""

    name: str
    slug: str


@post("/projects", component="Projects/Index", sync_to_thread=False)
@precognition
def create_project(request: Request[Any, Any, Any], data: Annotated[CreateProjectPayload, Body()]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate and create a project with Precognition and flash notifications."""
    share(request, "currentUser", AuthenticatedUser(id=7, email="ada@example.com", role="admin"))
    if data.slug == "reserved":
        error(request, "slug", "The 'reserved' slug is unavailable.")
        flash(request, "Please choose a different project slug.", category="error")
        return {"created": False}

    flash(request, f"Project '{data.name}' created.", category="success")
    return {"created": True, "slug": data.slug}


def create_app() -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar app with typed shared props and Precognition enabled."""
    vite_config = ViteConfig(
        mode="hybrid",
        dev_mode=True,
        inertia=InertiaConfig(
            root_template="index.html",
            precognition=True,
            extra_static_page_props={"environment": "staging"},
            shared_page_prop_types={"currentUser": AuthenticatedUser},
        ),
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(start_dev_server=False),
    )
    return Litestar(route_handlers=[create_project], plugins=[VitePlugin(config=vite_config)])


def main() -> None:
    """Verify ``InertiaConfig`` shared prop typing and Precognition registration."""
    app = create_app()
    plugin = app.plugins.get(VitePlugin)
    assert isinstance(plugin.config.inertia, InertiaConfig)
    assert plugin.config.inertia.precognition is True
    assert plugin.config.inertia.shared_page_prop_types == {"currentUser": AuthenticatedUser}


__all__ = ("AuthenticatedUser", "CreateProjectPayload", "create_app", "create_project", "main")
```

### Lazy Shared Props

You can pass prop wrappers (`lazy()`, `once()`, `defer()`, `always()`) to `share()` so expensive shared data is only evaluated when needed or cached across visits:

```python
from typing import Any
from litestar import Request
from litestar_vite.inertia import lazy, once, share


def attach_shared_context(request: Request[Any, Any, Any]) -> None:
    """Attach cached permissions and on-demand notification counts."""
    share(request, "permissions", once("permissions", lambda: ["orders:read", "orders:write"]))
    share(request, "unreadCount", lazy("unreadCount", lambda: 5))
```

---

## Static & Session-Backed Shared Props

In addition to calling `share()` per request, `InertiaConfig` supports declarative static and session-backed props:

| Option | Type | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extra_static_page_props` | `dict[str, Any]` | Merged into every Inertia response (e.g., `{"appEnv": "production"}`). |
| `extra_session_page_props` | `set[str]` | Keys automatically read from `request.session` and included in `props` when present. |
| **Built-in Shared Props** | `errors`, `csrf_token` | Automatically injected on every Inertia response (`errors` defaults to `{}`). |

!!! note
    During partial reloads (`only` / `except`), shared props are filtered by the client's requested keys just like handler props — unless wrapped in `always()`.

---

## Typing Shared Props

Props registered dynamically via `share(connection, key, value)` inside guards or middleware have no static return annotation on individual route handlers.

By declaring `InertiaConfig(shared_page_prop_types={"currentUser": AuthenticatedUser})`, Litestar Vite's OpenAPI/TypeScript generator registers `AuthenticatedUser` in the shared schema registry and emits the exact TypeScript type on `SharedPageProps` in `page-props.ts` — eliminating `unknown` or hand-maintained duplicate interfaces.

---

## Top-Level Flash Messages

Inertia v2.3+ places flash messages at the **top level** of the page object (`page.flash`) rather than inside `page.props.flash` so flash messages are never accidentally cached in `window.history.state` or re-triggered on Back/Forward navigation.

Call [`flash(connection, message, category="info")`](../../reference/inertia.md#litestar_vite.inertia.flash) on the server:

```python
from typing import Any
from litestar import Request, post
from litestar_vite.inertia import InertiaRedirect, flash


@post("/settings", sync_to_thread=False)
def save_settings(request: Request[Any, Any, Any]) -> InertiaRedirect:
    """Persist settings and stage a top-level flash message across the redirect."""
    flash(request, "Settings saved.", category="success")
    return InertiaRedirect(request, redirect_to="/settings")
```

### Reading Flash Messages on the Client

When `TypeGenConfig` runs (with `InertiaTypeGenConfig(include_default_flash=True)`), Litestar Vite generates `src/generated/inertia.d.ts` augmenting Inertia's `FlashDataType` with `FlashMessages` (`success?: string[]`, `error?: string[]`, `info?: string[]`, `warning?: string[]`):

=== "React"

    ```tsx title="resources/components/ToastBanner.tsx"
    import { usePage } from "@inertiajs/react";

    export function ToastBanner() {
      const page = usePage() as { flash?: Record<string, string[]> };
      const messages = page.flash?.success ?? [];

      if (!messages.length) return null;
      return (
        <div role="status" className="toast-success">
          {messages.map((msg, idx) => (
            <p key={idx}>{msg}</p>
          ))}
        </div>
      );
    }
    ```

=== "Vue 3"

    ```vue title="resources/components/ToastBanner.vue"
    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { computed } from "vue";
    import { usePage } from "@inertiajs/vue3";

    const page = usePage() as unknown as { flash?: Record<string, string[]> };
    const messages = computed(() => page.flash?.success ?? []);
    </script>

    <template>
      <div v-if="messages.length" role="status" class="toast-success">
        <p v-for="(msg, idx) in messages" :key="idx">{{ msg }}</p>
      </div>
    </template>
    ```

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/inertia/ssr-and-typescript.md -->

# SSR, TypeScript & Upgrade Guide

This guide covers Server-Side Rendering (`InertiaSSRConfig`), client helpers (`resolvePageComponent`, `unwrapPageProps`), end-to-end `PageProps` TypeScript generation, and Inertia v3 compatibility.

---

## Server-Side Rendering

Enabling `InertiaConfig(ssr=True)` (or `ssr=InertiaSSRConfig(...)`) pre-renders initial full-page Inertia visits on the server before returning HTML to the browser:

- **Development (`dev_mode=True`)**: Litestar sends the `PageProps` payload over `TCPStreamIPCTransport` to Vite's `/__litestar_ssr__` endpoint, which executes your `resources/ssr.tsx` (or `resources/ssr.ts`) entrypoint through Vite's `ModuleRunner` with full HMR invalidation.
- **Production (`dev_mode=False`)**: Litestar streams NDJSON requests over `StdioIPCTransport` to your compiled `ssr.js` worker (`startSsrWorker({ render })`).

```tsx title="resources/ssr.tsx"
import { createInertiaApp } from "@inertiajs/react";
import ReactDOMServer from "react-dom/server";
import { resolvePageComponent } from "litestar-vite-plugin/inertia-helpers";
import { startSsrWorker } from "litestar-vite-plugin/ssr-worker";

export default function render(page: unknown) {
  return createInertiaApp({
    page: page as never,
    render: ReactDOMServer.renderToString,
    defaults: {
      future: {
        useScriptElementForInitialPage: true,
      },
    },
    resolve: (name: string) =>
      resolvePageComponent(
        `./pages/${name}.tsx`,
        import.meta.glob("./pages/**/*.tsx", { eager: true }),
      ),
    setup: ({ App, props }: { App: any; props: any }) => <App {...props} />,
  });
}

startSsrWorker({ render });
```

### Bootstrap Interaction

When SSR returns `{ head, body }`, `inject_inertia_ssr_tags` splices `head` into `<!--inertia-head-->` (or `<head>`) and replaces `<div id="app">` (your configured `app_selector`) with the pre-rendered `body` while preserving `<script type="application/json" id="app_page" data-page="app">` when `use_script_element=True` (or the `data-page` attribute when `use_script_element=False`).

---

## Page Resolution & Prop Unwrapping Helpers

`litestar-vite-plugin/inertia-helpers` exports two zero-dependency utilities:

| Function | Signature | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`resolvePageComponent`](../../reference/typescript/helpers.md) | `resolvePageComponent(path, pages, options?): Promise<T>` | Resolves a page module from `import.meta.glob(...)` (eager or lazy), supporting fallback path arrays and descriptive errors when a component is missing. |
| [`unwrapPageProps`](../../reference/typescript/helpers.md) | `unwrapPageProps<T>(props: T): UnwrappedPageProps<T>` | Unwraps nested `{ content: ... }` envelopes when handlers wrap structured responses. |

---

## Automatic PageProps Type Generation

When `TypeGenConfig(generate_page_props=True)` is active, Litestar Vite inspects every route handler with a `component="..."` option (`extract_inertia_pages`), writes `.litestar/inertia-pages.json`, and generates `src/generated/page-props.ts`:

```typescript title="src/generated/page-props.ts (Generated)"
import type { InvoiceSummary } from "./api/types.gen";

export interface InvoicesIndexProps {
  invoices: InvoiceSummary[];
}

export interface PageProps {
  "Invoices/Index": InvoicesIndexProps;
  "Invoices/Show": InvoiceSummary;
}

export type InertiaPageProps<C extends keyof PageProps = keyof PageProps> =
  PageProps[C] & SharedPageProps;

export type PagePropsFor<C extends keyof PageProps> = InertiaPageProps<C>;
```

### Customizing User and SharedProps Types

Customize default `AuthData` or `SharedProps` in `src/types/inertia.d.ts` (or disable default auth generation with `InertiaTypeGenConfig(include_default_auth=False)`):

<!-- docs-example: skip -->
```typescript title="src/types/inertia.d.ts"
import "litestar-vite-plugin/inertia";

declare module "litestar-vite-plugin/inertia" {
  interface User {
    id: string;
    email: string;
    roles: ("admin" | "member")[];
  }

  interface SharedProps {
    tenantId: string;
  }
}
```

---

## Inertia v3 Compatibility

| Feature | Standard Inertia.js | Inertia v3 (`@inertiajs/*` v3) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Script-Element Bootstrap** | Opt-in on client via `defaults: { future: { useScriptElementForInitialPage: true } }` | **Default behavior** when `InertiaConfig(use_script_element=True)` is active (`defaults: {}`). |
| **Document `<title>` Tag** | `<title inertia>` or `<title data-inertia>` | Plain `<title>App</title>` (v3 replaces the single `<title>` element automatically without marker attributes). |
| **HTTP Client** | Axios | Native `fetch` / XHR (no `axios` dependency required). |
| **Top-Level Flash** | Supported (`page.flash`) | Standard (`page.flash`). |

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/nuxt.md -->

# Nuxt

Build full-stack Vue applications with [Nuxt](https://nuxt.com) and Litestar using the `litestar-vite-plugin/nuxt` module (`mode="ssr"` / `mode="framework"`).

---

## Quick Start

```bash
litestar assets init --template nuxt
litestar assets install
litestar run --reload
```

---

## Project Structure

```text
my-project/
├── app.py                  # Litestar API + ViteConfig(mode="ssr")
├── nuxt.config.ts          # Nuxt configuration with litestar-vite-plugin/nuxt
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── app.vue                 # Root Nuxt component
├── pages/
│   └── index.vue           # File-based Nuxt routes
└── generated/              # Auto-generated routes.ts, schemas.ts, api/
```

---

## Configuration

=== "Python (`app.py`)"

    ```python title="app.py"
    from pathlib import Path

    from litestar import Litestar, get
    from msgspec import Struct
    from litestar_vite import PathConfig, RuntimeConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


    class Summary(Struct):
        title: str
        headline: str


    @get("/api/summary", name="summary", sync_to_thread=False)
    def get_summary() -> Summary:
        """Return typed summary payload for Nuxt SSR and client fetches."""
        return Summary(title="Litestar + Nuxt", headline="Universal Vue Rendering & Typed API")


    app = Litestar(
        route_handlers=[get_summary],
        plugins=[
            VitePlugin(
                config=ViteConfig(
                    mode="ssr",
                    dev_mode=True,
                    paths=PathConfig(resource_dir=Path("."), bundle_dir=Path(".output/public")),
                    runtime=RuntimeConfig(executor="node"),
                    types=TypeGenConfig(output=Path("generated"), generate_sdk=True, generate_routes=True),
                ),
            ),
        ],
    )
    ```

=== "Nuxt (`nuxt.config.ts`)"

    ```typescript title="nuxt.config.ts"
    import litestarNuxt from "litestar-vite-plugin/nuxt";

    export default defineNuxtConfig({
      compatibilityDate: "2025-01-01",
      modules: [
        [
          litestarNuxt,
          {
            apiPrefix: "/api",
            types: "auto",
          },
        ],
      ],
    });
    ```

---

## Using `useFetch` with Generated `route`

In Nuxt pages and composables, combine `useFetch` with the generated `route()` helper for SSR-hydrated, type-safe data fetching:

```vue title="pages/index.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
import { route } from "~/generated/routes";
import type { Summary } from "~/generated/api";

declare function useFetch<T>(url: string): Promise<{ data: { value: T | null }; pending: { value: boolean } }>;

const { data: summary, pending } = await useFetch<Summary>(route("summary"));
</script>

<template>
  <main v-if="!pending && summary">
    <h1>{{ summary.title }}</h1>
    <p>{{ summary.headline }}</p>
  </main>
</template>
```

---

## Production Deployment

1. **Static Generation (`nuxt generate`)**: Outputs static HTML and client bundles to `.output/public`, which Litestar serves directly in production.
2. **Universal SSR (`nuxt build`)**: Outputs a Nitro server in `.output/server/index.mjs`; run Litestar and Nitro behind a reverse proxy or let Nitro proxy `/api/**` to Litestar via `routeRules`.

---
