# React

Build React applications with Litestar using Vite 7+, `@vitejs/plugin-react` Fast Refresh, automatic OpenAPI + route type generation, and reactive realtime hooks.

---

## Quick Start

Scaffold a React project with `litestar assets init`:

=== "React SPA"

    ```bash
    litestar assets init --template react
    litestar assets install
    litestar run --reload
    ```

=== "React + Inertia"

    ```bash
    litestar assets init --template react-inertia
    litestar assets install
    litestar run --reload
    ```

---

## Project Structure

```text
my-project/
├── app.py                  # Litestar application
├── index.html              # SPA HTML shell (root or resources/)
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── vite.config.ts          # Vite + @vitejs/plugin-react + litestar-vite-plugin
└── src/
    ├── main.tsx            # React root entrypoint
    ├── App.tsx             # Root component
    └── generated/          # Auto-generated routes.ts, schemas.ts, api/, channels.ts
```

---

## Configuration

=== "Python (`app.py`)"

    ```python title="app.py"
    from pathlib import Path

    from litestar import Litestar, get
    from msgspec import Struct
    from litestar_vite import PathConfig, RuntimeConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


    class Summary(Struct):
        title: str
        headline: str


    @get("/api/summary", name="summary", sync_to_thread=False)
    def get_summary() -> Summary:
        """Return typed summary payload."""
        return Summary(title="Litestar + React", headline="Fast Refresh & End-to-End Types")


    app = Litestar(
        route_handlers=[get_summary],
        plugins=[
            VitePlugin(
                config=ViteConfig(
                    mode="spa",
                    dev_mode=True,
                    paths=PathConfig(resource_dir=Path("src")),
                    runtime=RuntimeConfig(is_react=True),
                    types=TypeGenConfig(generate_sdk=True, generate_routes=True),
                ),
            ),
        ],
    )
    ```

=== "Vite (`vite.config.ts`)"

    ```typescript title="vite.config.ts"
    import path from "node:path";
    import { defineConfig } from "vite";
    import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
    import litestar from "litestar-vite-plugin";

    export default defineConfig({
      plugins: [
        react(),
        litestar({
          input: ["src/main.tsx"],
          types: "auto",
        }),
      ],
      resolve: {
        alias: {
          "@": path.resolve(__dirname, "./src"),
        },
      },
    });
    ```

=== "HTML Entry (`index.html`)"

    ```html title="index.html"
    <!doctype html>
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8" />
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
        <title>Litestar + React</title>
      </head>
      <body>
        <div id="root"></div>
        <script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx"></script>
      </body>
    </html>
    ```

---

## React Fast Refresh Preamble

Unlike Vue and Svelte, `@vitejs/plugin-react` requires an inline `<script type="module">` Fast Refresh preamble (`/@react-refresh`) in `<head>` before any `.tsx` or `.jsx` module executes in development:

- **Automatic Detection**: When `litestar-vite-plugin` detects `@vitejs/plugin-react` (or `@vitejs/plugin-react-swc`) in `vite.config.ts`, or when `RuntimeConfig(is_react=True)` is set in Python, `ViteAssetLoader.render_hmr_client()` and the SPA HTML transformer inject the React Fast Refresh preamble automatically.
- **Zero Production Overhead**: In production (`dev_mode=False`), no preamble is emitted.

---

## Consuming Generated Types & Routes

With `types=True` (or `TypeGenConfig()`), Litestar Vite generates both `routes.ts` and the `@hey-api/openapi-ts` client SDK under `src/generated/`:

```tsx title="src/App.tsx"
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { route } from "@/generated/routes";
import { getApiSummary, type Summary } from "@/generated/api";

export function App() {
  const [summary, setSummary] = useState<Summary | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    getApiSummary().then(({ data }: { data?: Summary }) => {
      if (data) setSummary(data);
    });
  }, []);

  if (!summary) return <p>Loading from {route("summary")}...</p>;

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{summary.title}</h1>
      <p>{summary.headline}</p>
    </main>
  );
}
```

---

## Realtime & Event Stream Hooks

Import `useEventStream` or `useQueueEventStream` from `litestar-vite-plugin/react` to subscribe to Server-Sent Events or Litestar Channels in React components with automatic reconnection and cleanup on unmount:

```tsx title="src/Notifications.tsx"
import { useEventStream } from "litestar-vite-plugin/react";

interface NotificationPayload {
  id: string;
  message: string;
}

export function Notifications() {
  const { healthy, lastEvent } = useEventStream<NotificationPayload>({
    key: "notifications",
    url: "/api/notifications/stream",
    onEvent: () => {},
  });

  return (
    <aside>
      <span>Stream healthy: {String(healthy)}</span>
      {lastEvent && <p>{lastEvent.message}</p>}
    </aside>
  );
}
```

See [Realtime Event Streams](../typegen/event-streams.md) for typed AsyncAPI channels, authentication tickets, and gap recovery.

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/svelte.md -->

# Svelte 5

Build Svelte 5 applications with Litestar using fine-grained runes (`$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`, `$props`), Vite 7+ HMR, and automatic TypeScript code generation.

---

## Quick Start

Scaffold a Svelte 5 project with `litestar assets init`:

=== "Svelte 5 SPA"

    ```bash
    litestar assets init --template svelte
    litestar assets install
    litestar run --reload
    ```

=== "Svelte 5 + Inertia"

    ```bash
    litestar assets init --template svelte-inertia
    litestar assets install
    litestar run --reload
    ```

---

## Project Structure

```text
my-project/
├── app.py                  # Litestar application
├── index.html              # SPA HTML shell
├── package.json
├── svelte.config.js        # vitePreprocess configuration
├── tsconfig.json
├── vite.config.ts          # Vite + @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte + litestar-vite-plugin
└── src/
    ├── main.ts             # Svelte 5 mount(App, ...) entrypoint
    ├── App.svelte          # Root Svelte 5 component
    └── generated/          # Auto-generated routes.ts, schemas.ts, api/, channels.ts
```

---

## Configuration

=== "Python (`app.py`)"

    ```python title="app.py"
    from pathlib import Path

    from litestar import Litestar, get
    from msgspec import Struct
    from litestar_vite import PathConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


    class Summary(Struct):
        title: str
        headline: str


    @get("/api/summary", name="summary", sync_to_thread=False)
    def get_summary() -> Summary:
        """Return typed summary payload."""
        return Summary(title="Litestar + Svelte 5", headline="Runes & End-to-End Types")


    app = Litestar(
        route_handlers=[get_summary],
        plugins=[
            VitePlugin(
                config=ViteConfig(
                    mode="spa",
                    dev_mode=True,
                    paths=PathConfig(resource_dir=Path("src")),
                    types=TypeGenConfig(generate_sdk=True, generate_routes=True),
                ),
            ),
        ],
    )
    ```

=== "Vite (`vite.config.ts`)"

    ```typescript title="vite.config.ts"
    import { defineConfig } from "vite";
    import { svelte } from "@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte";
    import litestar from "litestar-vite-plugin";

    export default defineConfig({
      plugins: [
        svelte(),
        litestar({
          input: ["src/main.ts"],
          types: "auto",
        }),
      ],
    });
    ```

=== "Svelte 5 Entry (`src/main.ts`)"

    ```typescript title="src/main.ts"
    import { mount } from "svelte";
    import App from "./App.svelte";

    const target = document.getElementById("app");
    if (!target) {
      throw new Error("Root element #app not found");
    }

    export default mount(App, { target });
    ```

---

## Svelte 5 Runes with Generated Types

Svelte 5 components use `$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`, and `$props()` alongside generated `route()` and SDK functions:

```svelte title="src/App.svelte"
<script lang="ts">
  import { route } from "./generated/routes";
  import { getApiSummary, type Summary } from "./generated/api";

  let summary = $state<Summary | null>(null);
  let loading = $state(true);
  const endpointUrl = route("summary");

  $effect(() => {
    getApiSummary().then(({ data }: { data?: Summary }) => {
      if (data) summary = data;
      loading = false;
    });
  });
</script>

{#if loading}
  <p>Loading from {endpointUrl}...</p>
{:else if summary}
  <main>
    <h1>{summary.title}</h1>
    <p>{summary.headline}</p>
  </main>
{/if}
```

---

## Realtime Stores

`litestar-vite-plugin/svelte` exports Svelte-compatible readable stores (`createEventStreamStore` and `createQueueEventStreamStore`) that automatically connect on first subscriber (`$store`) and close when the last subscriber unsubscribes:

```svelte title="src/Notifications.svelte"
<script lang="ts">
  import { createEventStreamStore } from "litestar-vite-plugin/svelte";

  interface NotificationPayload {
    id: string;
    message: string;
  }

  const stream = createEventStreamStore<NotificationPayload>({
    url: "/api/notifications/stream",
    onEvent: () => {},
  });
</script>

<aside>
  <span>Healthy: {$stream.healthy}</span>
  {#if $stream.lastEvent}
    <p>{$stream.lastEvent.message}</p>
  {/if}
</aside>
```

See [Realtime Event Streams](../typegen/event-streams.md) for typed AsyncAPI channels and stream presets.

---

<!-- Source: docs/frameworks/sveltekit.md -->

# SvelteKit

Build full-stack Svelte 5 applications with [SvelteKit](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit) and Litestar using `litestarSvelteKit()` from `litestar-vite-plugin/sveltekit`.

---

## Quick Start

```bash
litestar assets init --template sveltekit
litestar assets install
litestar run --reload
```

---

## Project Structure

```text
my-project/
├── app.py                  # Litestar API + ViteConfig(mode="ssr")
├── package.json
├── svelte.config.js        # @sveltejs/adapter-node configuration
├── tsconfig.json
├── vite.config.ts          # litestarSvelteKit() + sveltekit()
└── src/
    ├── app.html
    ├── hooks.server.ts     # Server-side /api/* proxy forwarding during SSR load()
    ├── lib/
    │   └── generated/      # Auto-generated routes.ts, schemas.ts, api/
    └── routes/
        ├── +layout.svelte
        ├── +page.ts        # Universal load function using route()
        └── +page.svelte
```

---

## Configuration

!!! important
    Register `litestarSvelteKit()` **before** `sveltekit()` in `vite.config.ts` so the `/api` proxy middleware runs before SvelteKit's catch-all route matcher.

=== "Python (`app.py`)"

    ```python title="app.py"
    from pathlib import Path

    from litestar import Litestar, get
    from msgspec import Struct
    from litestar_vite import PathConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


    class Summary(Struct):
        title: str
        headline: str


    @get("/api/summary", name="summary", sync_to_thread=False)
    def get_summary() -> Summary:
        """Return typed summary payload for SvelteKit load functions."""
        return Summary(title="Litestar + SvelteKit", headline="Typed Load Functions & Svelte 5 Runes")


    app = Litestar(
        route_handlers=[get_summary],
        plugins=[
            VitePlugin(
                config=ViteConfig(
                    mode="ssr",
                    dev_mode=True,
                    paths=PathConfig(resource_dir=Path("src"), bundle_dir=Path("build")),
                    types=TypeGenConfig(output=Path("src/lib/generated"), generate_sdk=True, generate_routes=True),
                ),
            ),
        ],
    )
    ```

=== "Vite (`vite.config.ts`)"

    ```typescript title="vite.config.ts"
    import { sveltekit } from "@sveltejs/kit/vite";
    import { defineConfig } from "vite";
    import { litestarSvelteKit } from "litestar-vite-plugin/sveltekit";

    export default defineConfig({
      plugins: [
        litestarSvelteKit({
          apiPrefix: "/api",
          types: "auto",
        }),
        sveltekit(),
      ],
    });
    ```

---

## Typed Load Functions

Use SvelteKit's universal `load` function (`+page.ts`) with the generated `route()` helper so both SSR and client-side navigations fetch typed data from Litestar:

=== "`src/routes/+page.ts`"

    <!-- docs-example: skip -->
    ```typescript title="src/routes/+page.ts"
    import { route } from "$lib/generated/routes";
    import type { Summary } from "$lib/generated/api";
    import type { PageLoad } from "./$types";

    export const load: PageLoad = async ({ fetch }) => {
      const response = await fetch(route("summary"));
      const summary = (await response.json()) as Summary;
      return { summary };
    };
    ```

=== "`src/routes/+page.svelte`"

    <!-- docs-example: skip -->
    ```svelte title="src/routes/+page.svelte"
    <script lang="ts">
      import type { PageProps } from "./$types";

      let { data }: PageProps = $props();
    </script>

    <main>
      <h1>{data.summary.title}</h1>
      <p>{data.summary.headline}</p>
    </main>
    ```

For general SvelteKit routing, adapters (`@sveltejs/adapter-node`, `@sveltejs/adapter-static`), and hooks, see the official [SvelteKit documentation](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit).

---

# Vue 3

Build Vue 3 applications with Litestar using Single-File Components (`.vue`), the Composition API (`<script setup lang="ts">`), Vite 7+ HMR, and end-to-end TypeScript codegen.

---

## Quick Start

Scaffold a Vue 3 project with `litestar assets init`:

=== "Vue 3 SPA"

    ```bash
    litestar assets init --template vue
    litestar assets install
    litestar run --reload
    ```

=== "Vue 3 + Inertia"

    ```bash
    litestar assets init --template vue-inertia
    litestar assets install
    litestar run --reload
    ```

=== "Vue 3 + Inertia SSR"

    ```bash
    litestar assets init --template vue-inertia-ssr
    litestar assets install
    litestar run --reload
    ```

---

## Project Structure

```text
my-project/
├── app.py                  # Litestar application
├── index.html              # SPA HTML shell
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── vite.config.ts          # Vite + @vitejs/plugin-vue + litestar-vite-plugin
└── src/
    ├── main.ts             # Vue createApp entrypoint
    ├── App.vue             # Root Single-File Component
    └── generated/          # Auto-generated routes.ts, schemas.ts, api/, channels.ts
```

---

## Configuration

=== "Python (`app.py`)"

    ```python title="app.py"
    from pathlib import Path

    from litestar import Litestar, get
    from msgspec import Struct
    from litestar_vite import PathConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


    class Summary(Struct):
        title: str
        headline: str


    @get("/api/summary", name="summary", sync_to_thread=False)
    def get_summary() -> Summary:
        """Return typed summary payload."""
        return Summary(title="Litestar + Vue 3", headline="Composition API & Typed Routes")


    app = Litestar(
        route_handlers=[get_summary],
        plugins=[
            VitePlugin(
                config=ViteConfig(
                    mode="spa",
                    dev_mode=True,
                    paths=PathConfig(resource_dir=Path("src")),
                    types=TypeGenConfig(generate_sdk=True, generate_routes=True),
                ),
            ),
        ],
    )
    ```

=== "Vite (`vite.config.ts`)"

    ```typescript title="vite.config.ts"
    import path from "node:path";
    import { defineConfig } from "vite";
    import vue from "@vitejs/plugin-vue";
    import litestar from "litestar-vite-plugin";

    export default defineConfig({
      plugins: [
        vue(),
        litestar({
          input: ["src/main.ts"],
          types: "auto",
        }),
      ],
      resolve: {
        alias: {
          "@": path.resolve(__dirname, "./src"),
        },
      },
    });
    ```

=== "Vue Entry (`src/main.ts`)"

    ```typescript title="src/main.ts"
    import { createApp } from "vue";
    import App from "./App.vue";

    createApp(App).mount("#app");
    ```

---

## Single-File Component with Generated Types

Use `<script setup lang="ts">` to import generated routes (`route()`) and OpenAPI SDK functions directly inside `.vue` components:

```vue title="src/App.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, ref } from "vue";
import { route } from "@/generated/routes";
import { getApiSummary, type Summary } from "@/generated/api";

const summary = ref<Summary | null>(null);
const endpointUrl = route("summary");

onMounted(async () => {
  const { data } = await getApiSummary();
  if (data) {
    summary.value = data;
  }
});
</script>

<template>
  <main v-if="summary">
    <h1>{{ summary.title }}</h1>
    <p>{{ summary.headline }}</p>
  </main>
  <p v-else>Fetching {{ endpointUrl }}...</p>
</template>
```

---

## Realtime Composables

`litestar-vite-plugin/vue` exports Vue 3 Composition API composables (`useEventStream` and `useQueueEventStream`) returning reactive `Readonly<Ref<...>>` handles that automatically close when the enclosing component unmounts:

```vue title="src/Notifications.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useEventStream } from "litestar-vite-plugin/vue";

interface NotificationPayload {
  id: string;
  message: string;
}

const { healthy, lastEvent } = useEventStream<NotificationPayload>({
  key: "notifications",
  url: "/api/notifications/stream",
  onEvent: () => {},
});
</script>

<template>
  <aside>
    <span>Stream healthy: {{ healthy }}</span>
    <p v-if="lastEvent">{{ lastEvent.message }}</p>
  </aside>
</template>
```

See [Realtime Event Streams](../typegen/event-streams.md) and [Inertia Overview](inertia/index.md) for server-driven Vue 3 patterns.

---

<!-- Source: docs/getting-started/index.md -->

# Getting Started

Litestar Vite pairs two packages that work together across the `.litestar.json` contract:

- **Litestar Vite** (Python): The Litestar plugin (`VitePlugin`), configuration models (`ViteConfig`), AnyIO dev proxy (`ViteProxyMiddleware`), Inertia.js protocol engine, fragment renderer, and `litestar assets` CLI.
- **`litestar-vite-plugin`** (TypeScript): The Vite 7+ plugin that reads `.litestar.json`, writes `<bundle_dir>/hot`, runs `@hey-api/openapi-ts` and AsyncAPI codegen, and registers the dev SSR / fragment RPC middleware (`/__litestar_ssr__`).

---

## Installation

Install the Python package in your backend environment:

=== "uv"

    ```bash
    uv add litestar-vite
    ```

=== "pip"

    ```bash
    pip install litestar-vite
    ```

=== "pdm"

    ```bash
    pdm add litestar-vite
    ```

=== "poetry"

    ```bash
    poetry add litestar-vite
    ```

!!! tip "Optional Extras (`jinja`, `asyncapi`, `node`, `bun`, `deno`, `wasm`)"
    - **Jinja2 templates (`mode="template"`)**: `uv add "litestar-vite[jinja]"`
    - **AsyncAPI channel codegen (`generate_channels=True`)**: `uv add "litestar-vite[asyncapi]"`
    - **Self-contained JS runtime wheels (no host Node/Bun/Deno needed)**: `uv add "litestar-vite[node]"`, `"litestar-vite[bun]"`, or `"litestar-vite[deno]"`
    - **In-process QuickJS SSR (`WasmIPCTransport`)**: `uv add "litestar-vite[wasm]"`

Install the Vite plugin in your frontend directory (`package.json`):

=== "npm"

    ```bash
    npm install -D litestar-vite-plugin
    ```

=== "pnpm"

    ```bash
    pnpm add -D litestar-vite-plugin
    ```

=== "bun"

    ```bash
    bun add -d litestar-vite-plugin
    ```

---

## Scaffolding a New Frontend

The fastest way to bootstrap a new frontend workspace is `litestar assets init`, which generates `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, and framework entrypoints aligned with your `ViteConfig`:

```console
$ litestar assets init --template react-inertia
✓ Created vite.config.ts, package.json, tsconfig.json
✓ Created resources/main.tsx and resources/pages/Home.tsx
$ litestar assets install
✓ Frontend dependencies installed
$ litestar run --reload
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
```

### Available Scaffolding Templates

| Template Flag (`--template`) | Operating Mode | Stack |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `react` | `mode="spa"` | React + TypeScript + Vite 7+ |
| `vue` | `mode="spa"` | Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite 7+ |
| `svelte` | `mode="spa"` | Svelte 5 + TypeScript + Vite 7+ |
| `angular` | `mode="spa"` | Angular + `@analogjs/vite-plugin-angular` |
| `angular-cli` | `mode="external"` | Angular CLI (`@angular/build`) + Litestar proxy |
| `react-inertia` | `mode="hybrid"` | React + `@inertiajs/react` |
| `vue-inertia` | `mode="hybrid"` | Vue 3 + `@inertiajs/vue3` |
| `svelte-inertia` | `mode="hybrid"` | Svelte 5 + `@inertiajs/svelte` |
| `htmx` | `mode="htmx"` | Jinja2 + HTMX + `registerHtmxExtension()` |
| `astro` | `mode="ssg"` | Astro + `litestar-vite-plugin/astro` |
| `nuxt` | `mode="ssr"` | Nuxt + `litestar-vite-plugin/nuxt` |
| `sveltekit` | `mode="ssr"` | SvelteKit + `litestar-vite-plugin/sveltekit` |

---

## Pick Your Quick-Start Walkthrough

Choose the walkthrough that matches your architecture:

1. [**Quick Start: Single-Page Application (`mode="spa"`)**](quick-start-spa.md) — Litestar serves JSON/OpenAPI routes and injects Vite scripts into `index.html` for a client-routed SPA.
2. [**Quick Start: Inertia.js (`mode="hybrid"`)**](quick-start-inertia.md) — Server-driven routing with React, Vue, or Svelte page components and typed `PageProps`.
3. [**Quick Start: Jinja2 Templates & Islands (`mode="template"`)**](quick-start-templates.md) — Server-rendered HTML templates with `vite_hmr()`, `vite()`, `<litestar-island>` hydration, and HTMX `ComponentResponse` fragments.

---

<!-- Source: docs/getting-started/quick-start-inertia.md -->

# Quick Start: Inertia.js

In **Inertia Hybrid mode** (`mode="hybrid"`), Litestar owns server-side routing, authentication, and data loading while React, Vue, or Svelte renders each page component. Route handlers declare `component="Dashboard/Index"` and return a Python `dict` or `msgspec.Struct` directly — no client REST or GraphQL boilerplate required.

---

## Install Dependencies

=== "uv"

    ```bash
    uv add litestar-vite
    ```

=== "pip"

    ```bash
    pip install litestar-vite
    ```

=== "pdm"

    ```bash
    pdm add litestar-vite
    ```

=== "poetry"

    ```bash
    poetry add litestar-vite
    ```

Install `litestar-vite-plugin` and your Inertia.js adapter:

=== "npm"

    ```bash
    npm install -D litestar-vite-plugin
    npm install @inertiajs/react react react-dom
    ```

=== "pnpm"

    ```bash
    pnpm add -D litestar-vite-plugin
    pnpm add @inertiajs/react react react-dom
    ```

=== "bun"

    ```bash
    bun add -d litestar-vite-plugin
    bun add @inertiajs/react react react-dom
    ```

---

## Configure Litestar

Set `mode="hybrid"` and configure `InertiaConfig(root_template="index.html")`. When `mode="hybrid"` is active, `VitePlugin` automatically activates `InertiaPlugin` and `InertiaMiddleware`:

```python title="docs/examples/getting_started/inertia_app.py"
"""Inertia.js v2 Hybrid Mode quick-start example with Litestar and Vite."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from litestar import Litestar, get
from msgspec import Struct

from litestar_vite import InertiaConfig, PathConfig, RuntimeConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


class ProjectItem(Struct, frozen=True, gc=False):
    """Project summary rendered inside an Inertia page component."""

    id: int
    name: str
    status: str


@get("/", component="Dashboard/Index", sync_to_thread=False)
def dashboard() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return Inertia page props for the ``Dashboard/Index`` component."""
    return {
        "projects": [
            ProjectItem(id=1, name="Litestar API", status="healthy"),
            ProjectItem(id=2, name="Vite Asset Pipeline", status="building"),
        ]
    }


def create_app() -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar application configured for Inertia v2 hybrid mode."""
    vite_config = ViteConfig(
        mode="hybrid",
        dev_mode=True,
        paths=PathConfig(root=Path(), resource_dir=Path("resources"), bundle_dir=Path("public/build")),
        inertia=InertiaConfig(root_template="index.html"),
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(start_dev_server=False),
    )
    return Litestar(route_handlers=[dashboard], plugins=[VitePlugin(config=vite_config)])


def main() -> None:
    """Verify the Inertia hybrid application constructs cleanly."""
    app = create_app()
    plugin = app.plugins.get(VitePlugin)
    assert plugin.config.mode == "hybrid"
    assert ProjectItem(id=1, name="Litestar API", status="healthy").status == "healthy"


__all__ = ("ProjectItem", "create_app", "dashboard", "main")
```

---

## Create the Root HTML Shell and Client Entrypoint

In `mode="hybrid"`, `index.html` needs only `<div id="app"></div>` and your module entrypoint. By default (`InertiaConfig(use_script_element=True)`), Litestar Vite injects `<script type="application/json" data-page="app">{...}</script>` right before `<div id="app"></div>`:

```html title="index.html"
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>Litestar + Inertia.js</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="app"></div>
    <script type="module" src="/resources/main.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

Initialize Inertia in `resources/main.tsx` using `resolvePageComponent` from `litestar-vite-plugin/inertia-helpers` and enable `useScriptElementForInitialPage: true`:

```tsx title="resources/main.tsx"
import { createInertiaApp } from "@inertiajs/react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { resolvePageComponent } from "litestar-vite-plugin/inertia-helpers";

createInertiaApp({
  defaults: {
    future: {
      useScriptElementForInitialPage: true,
    },
  },
  resolve: (name: string) =>
    resolvePageComponent(
      `./pages/${name}.tsx`,
      import.meta.glob("./pages/**/*.tsx"),
    ),
  setup({ el, App, props }: { el: HTMLElement; App: any; props: any }) {
    createRoot(el).render(<App {...props} />);
  },
});
```

---

## Run and Navigate

Start Litestar and Vite together:

```bash
litestar run --reload
```

- On initial visit to `GET /`, Litestar renders `index.html` with the initial `PageProps` JSON and Vite asset scripts.
- On subsequent `<Link href="...">` clicks, Inertia sends `X-Inertia: true` and swaps only the JSON `PageProps` payload.
- See the [Inertia.js Guide](../frameworks/inertia/index.md) for deferred props (`defer`), infinite scroll (`merge`), shared session data (`share`), and SSR.

---

<!-- Source: docs/getting-started/quick-start-spa.md -->

# Quick Start: Single-Page Application

In **SPA mode** (`mode="spa"`), Litestar owns your JSON API routes and serves a transformed `index.html` shell for all unmatched non-API GET routes via `AppHandler`. Your frontend router (`react-router`, `vue-router`, or TanStack Router) handles client-side navigation while `TypeGenConfig` generates a fully typed TypeScript SDK from Litestar's OpenAPI schema.

---

## Install Dependencies

=== "uv"

    ```bash
    uv add litestar-vite
    ```

=== "pip"

    ```bash
    pip install litestar-vite
    ```

=== "pdm"

    ```bash
    pdm add litestar-vite
    ```

=== "poetry"

    ```bash
    poetry add litestar-vite
    ```

And in your frontend workspace:

=== "npm"

    ```bash
    npm install -D litestar-vite-plugin @hey-api/openapi-ts
    ```

=== "pnpm"

    ```bash
    pnpm add -D litestar-vite-plugin @hey-api/openapi-ts
    ```

=== "bun"

    ```bash
    bun add -d litestar-vite-plugin @hey-api/openapi-ts
    ```

---

## Configure Litestar

Register `VitePlugin` with `mode="spa"` and enable `TypeGenConfig` so Litestar exports `openapi.json` and `routes.json` on startup:

```python title="docs/examples/getting_started/spa_app.py"
"""Single-Page Application (SPA) quick-start example with Litestar and Vite."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from litestar import Litestar, get
from msgspec import Struct

from litestar_vite import PathConfig, RuntimeConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


class SummaryStats(Struct, frozen=True, gc=False):
    """Dashboard summary payload returned by the JSON API."""

    active_users: int
    requests_per_second: float
    region: str


@get("/api/summary", sync_to_thread=False)
def get_summary() -> SummaryStats:
    """Return typed summary metrics for the SPA frontend."""
    return SummaryStats(active_users=128, requests_per_second=412.5, region="us-east-1")


def create_app() -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar application configured for SPA mode."""
    vite_config = ViteConfig(
        mode="spa",
        dev_mode=True,
        paths=PathConfig(root=Path(), resource_dir=Path("src"), bundle_dir=Path("public/build")),
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(start_dev_server=False),
        types=TypeGenConfig(generate_sdk=True, generate_routes=True),
    )
    return Litestar(route_handlers=[get_summary], plugins=[VitePlugin(config=vite_config)])


def main() -> None:
    """Verify the SPA example application constructs cleanly."""
    app = create_app()
    plugin = app.plugins.get(VitePlugin)
    assert plugin.config.mode == "spa"
    assert SummaryStats(active_users=128, requests_per_second=412.5, region="us-east-1").active_users == 128


__all__ = ("SummaryStats", "create_app", "get_summary", "main")
```

---

## Configure Vite

Point `litestar-vite-plugin` at your application entrypoint (`src/main.tsx` or `src/main.ts`). All path, port, and typegen settings are automatically synchronized from `.litestar.json`:

```typescript title="vite.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import litestar from "litestar-vite-plugin";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    react(),
    litestar({
      input: ["src/main.tsx"],
    }),
  ],
});
```

---

## Create the HTML Shell and Run

Place `index.html` in your project root (or `resource_dir`). In `mode="spa"`, `AppHandler` automatically injects `@vite/client` (and the React Fast Refresh preamble when `is_react=True`) in development, and swaps in hashed `manifest.json` bundle tags in production:

```html title="index.html"
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>Litestar SPA</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="app"></div>
    <script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

Start the unified development server:

```bash
litestar run --reload
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000` in your browser:

- `GET /api/summary` returns the JSON `SummaryStats` response from Litestar.
- `GET /` (and any client route like `/settings`) serves the transformed `index.html` shell.
- `/src/main.tsx` and `/vite-hmr` stream through `ViteProxyMiddleware` over port `8000`.

---

<!-- Source: docs/getting-started/quick-start-templates.md -->

# Quick Start: Jinja2 Templates & Islands

In **Template mode** (`mode="template"`), Litestar renders server-side Jinja2 templates while `VitePlugin` registers template callables (`vite_hmr()`, `vite()`, `vite_fragment()`, `vite_static()`) and mounts `<litestar-island>` web components or HTMX `ComponentResponse` fragments.

---

## Install Dependencies

Install Litestar Vite with the `jinja` extra:

=== "uv"

    ```bash
    uv add "litestar-vite[jinja]"
    ```

=== "pip"

    ```bash
    pip install "litestar-vite[jinja]"
    ```

=== "pdm"

    ```bash
    pdm add "litestar-vite[jinja]"
    ```

=== "poetry"

    ```bash
    poetry add "litestar-vite[jinja]"
    ```

Install `litestar-vite-plugin` in your frontend workspace:

=== "npm"

    ```bash
    npm install -D litestar-vite-plugin
    ```

=== "pnpm"

    ```bash
    pnpm add -D litestar-vite-plugin
    ```

=== "bun"

    ```bash
    bun add -d litestar-vite-plugin
    ```

---

## Configure Litestar

Configure `TemplateConfig(engine=JinjaTemplateEngine)` alongside `VitePlugin(config=ViteConfig(mode="template"))`. Route handlers can return standard `Template` responses for full pages or `ComponentResponse` for partial HTMX swaps:

```python title="docs/examples/getting_started/template_app.py"
"""Jinja2 server-rendered templates with Vite assets and interactive islands."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from litestar import Litestar, get
from litestar.plugins.jinja import JinjaTemplateEngine
from litestar.response import Template
from litestar.template.config import TemplateConfig

from litestar_vite import ComponentResponse, PathConfig, RuntimeConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


@get("/", sync_to_thread=False)
def home_page() -> Template:
    """Render a server-driven Jinja2 template with Vite asset tags."""
    return Template(template_name="home.html.j2", context={"title": "Orders Overview", "initial_count": 42})


@get("/fragments/metrics-card", sync_to_thread=False)
def metrics_fragment() -> ComponentResponse:
    """Return a pre-rendered UI component fragment for HTMX swap targets."""
    return ComponentResponse(component="components/MetricsCard.tsx", props={"activeOrders": 42, "latencyMs": 11.4})


def create_app(templates_dir: Path | None = None) -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar application in ``template`` mode with Jinja2."""
    resolved_dir = templates_dir or Path()
    vite_config = ViteConfig(
        mode="template",
        dev_mode=True,
        paths=PathConfig(root=Path(), resource_dir=Path("resources"), bundle_dir=Path("public/build")),
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(start_dev_server=False),
    )
    return Litestar(
        route_handlers=[home_page, metrics_fragment],
        template_config=TemplateConfig(directory=resolved_dir, engine=JinjaTemplateEngine),
        plugins=[VitePlugin(config=vite_config)],
    )


def main() -> None:
    """Verify the template mode application and component fragment response."""
    app = create_app()
    plugin = app.plugins.get(VitePlugin)
    assert plugin.config.mode == "template"
    fragment = ComponentResponse(component="components/MetricsCard.tsx", props={"activeOrders": 42, "latencyMs": 11.4})
    assert fragment.component == "components/MetricsCard.tsx"
    assert fragment.props["activeOrders"] == 42


__all__ = ("create_app", "home_page", "main", "metrics_fragment")
```

---

## Author the Jinja2 Template

Use `{{ vite_hmr() }}` and `{{ vite('resources/main.ts') }}` in `<head>`, and embed interactive islands with `{{ vite_fragment('components/MetricsCard.tsx', props={'activeOrders': initial_count}, hydrate='visible') }}`:

```html title="home.html.j2"
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <title>{{ title }}</title>
    {{ vite_hmr() }}
    {{ vite('resources/main.ts') }}
  </head>
  <body>
    <main>
      <h1>{{ title }}</h1>
      {{ vite_fragment(
          'components/MetricsCard.tsx',
          props={'activeOrders': initial_count, 'latencyMs': 11.4},
          hydrate='visible'
      ) }}
      <button
        hx-get="/fragments/metrics-card"
        hx-target="#live-metrics"
        hx-swap="innerHTML">
        Refresh Metrics
      </button>
      <div id="live-metrics"></div>
    </main>
  </body>
</html>
```

---

## Register Island Hydration

Register the `<litestar-island>` custom element in your client entrypoint so islands hydrate according to their `data-hydrate` strategy (`load`, `idle`, `visible`, or `media`):

```typescript title="resources/main.ts"
import { hydrateIslands } from "litestar-vite-plugin/fragments/client";
import { hydrateReact } from "litestar-vite-plugin/fragments/react";

hydrateIslands({
  "islands/RevenueChart": {
    load: () => import("./islands/RevenueChart"),
    hydrate: hydrateReact,
  },
});
```

See [Islands Architecture & HTMX Integration](../learn/islands-and-htmx.md) for the complete lifecycle of `vite_fragment()`, `<litestar-island>`, and `ComponentResponse`.

<div class="lv-home-hero" align="center">
  <img class="lv-hero-banner lv-hero-banner--light" alt="Litestar Vite" src="assets/banner-inline-light.svg">
  <img class="lv-hero-banner lv-hero-banner--dark" alt="Litestar Vite" src="assets/banner-inline-dark.svg">
  <p><strong>First-class Vite 7+, Inertia.js, Server-Rendered Islands, and End-to-End Type Generation for Litestar.</strong></p>
</div>

---

**Litestar Vite** bridges [Litestar](https://litestar.dev) (Python ASGI) and [Vite 7+](https://vite.dev) into a unified full-stack runtime. During development, your browser connects solely to Litestar (`:8000`) while the single-port proxy streams frontend modules and hot-reload WebSocket updates from a managed Vite process. In production, the asset loader serves hashed, immutable bundles directly from the Vite manifest.

[Interactive Architecture Diagram: diagram-dev-proxy.html]
---

## Choose Your Operating Mode

Litestar Vite adapts to your frontend architecture through a single mode setting on `ViteConfig`:

<div class="grid cards" markdown>

-   :lucide-layout-grid: **Single-Page Application**

    ---

    Litestar serves your JSON and OpenAPI routes while transforming `index.html` with Vite asset tags for React, Vue, Svelte, or Angular SPAs.

    [→ Quick Start: SPA](getting-started/quick-start-spa.md)

-   :lucide-repeat: **Inertia.js Hybrid**

    ---

    Build React, Vue, or Svelte single-page applications without maintaining a separate client API layer. Return Python models directly as typed page props.

    [→ Quick Start: Inertia.js](getting-started/quick-start-inertia.md)

-   :lucide-blocks: **Jinja2 & Islands**

    ---

    Render server-side Jinja2 templates enhanced with Vite HMR, interactive island hydration, and server component fragments for HTMX swaps.

    [→ Quick Start: Templates & Islands](getting-started/quick-start-templates.md)

-   :lucide-globe: **Meta-Frameworks**

    ---

    Run Astro, Nuxt, or SvelteKit behind Litestar's reverse proxy with automatic OpenAPI SDK, route helper, and AsyncAPI channel generation.

    [→ Astro](frameworks/astro.md) · [Nuxt](frameworks/nuxt.md) · [SvelteKit](frameworks/sveltekit.md)

</div>

---

## Installation and Setup

### Install the Python and Vite Packages

=== "uv"

    ```bash
    uv add litestar-vite
    ```

=== "pip"

    ```bash
    pip install litestar-vite
    ```

=== "pdm"

    ```bash
    pdm add litestar-vite
    ```

=== "poetry"

    ```bash
    poetry add litestar-vite
    ```

Install the paired Vite 7+ plugin in your frontend workspace:

=== "npm"

    ```bash
    npm install -D litestar-vite-plugin
    ```

=== "pnpm"

    ```bash
    pnpm add -D litestar-vite-plugin
    ```

=== "bun"

    ```bash
    bun add -d litestar-vite-plugin
    ```

### Register the Plugin on Your Litestar App

```python title="docs/examples/getting_started/spa_app.py"
"""Single-Page Application (SPA) quick-start example with Litestar and Vite."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from litestar import Litestar, get
from msgspec import Struct

from litestar_vite import PathConfig, RuntimeConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig, VitePlugin


class SummaryStats(Struct, frozen=True, gc=False):
    """Dashboard summary payload returned by the JSON API."""

    active_users: int
    requests_per_second: float
    region: str


@get("/api/summary", sync_to_thread=False)
def get_summary() -> SummaryStats:
    """Return typed summary metrics for the SPA frontend."""
    return SummaryStats(active_users=128, requests_per_second=412.5, region="us-east-1")


def create_app() -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar application configured for SPA mode."""
    vite_config = ViteConfig(
        mode="spa",
        dev_mode=True,
        paths=PathConfig(root=Path(), resource_dir=Path("src"), bundle_dir=Path("public/build")),
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(start_dev_server=False),
        types=TypeGenConfig(generate_sdk=True, generate_routes=True),
    )
    return Litestar(route_handlers=[get_summary], plugins=[VitePlugin(config=vite_config)])


def main() -> None:
    """Verify the SPA example application constructs cleanly."""
    app = create_app()
    plugin = app.plugins.get(VitePlugin)
    assert plugin.config.mode == "spa"
    assert SummaryStats(active_users=128, requests_per_second=412.5, region="us-east-1").active_users == 128


__all__ = ("SummaryStats", "create_app", "get_summary", "main")
```

### Scaffold and Run on a Single Port

```console
$ litestar assets init --template react
✓ Created vite.config.ts, package.json, tsconfig.json
$ litestar assets install
✓ Frontend dependencies installed
$ litestar run --reload
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
INFO:     Vite dev server started on http://127.0.0.1:5173 (proxied via :8000)
```

When `litestar run --reload` starts:

1. `VitePlugin` writes `.litestar.json` (the configuration bridge read by the Vite plugin) and exports OpenAPI and route schemas when type generation is enabled.
2. `VitePlugin` spawns the Vite dev server and reads its bound address from the `hot` file in your bundle directory.
3. Every browser request hits `http://127.0.0.1:8000` — Python API routes execute in Litestar, while Vite asset and HMR WebSocket traffic streams transparently through the single-port proxy.

# Configuration & Runtime Bridge

Litestar Vite organizes its configuration into a root [`ViteConfig`](../reference/plugin-and-config.md#litestar_vite.config.ViteConfig) object backed by five focused sub-configurations. At application startup, `ViteConfig` serializes a deterministic `.litestar.json` runtime bridge file that `litestar-vite-plugin` reads automatically in TypeScript.

---

## Layered Configuration Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    VC["ViteConfig"] --> PC["PathConfig\n(root, resource_dir, bundle_dir)"]
    VC --> RC["RuntimeConfig\n(dev_mode, proxy_mode, executor)"]
    VC --> IC["InertiaConfig\n(root_template, ssr, precognition)"]
    VC --> TC["TypeGenConfig\n(output, openapi, routes, asyncapi)"]
    VC --> DC["DeployConfig\n(storage_backend, asset_url)"]
    VC ==>|"Startup Export"| LJ[".litestar.json"]
    LJ ==>|"Read by Vite"| LVP["litestar-vite-plugin"]
```

| Config Class | Responsibility | Key Fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`ViteConfig`](../reference/plugin-and-config.md#litestar_vite.config.ViteConfig) | Top-level mode, environment, and sub-config composition | `mode`, `dev_mode`, `paths`, `runtime`, `inertia`, `types`, `deploy`, `static_props` |
| [`PathConfig`](../reference/plugin-and-config.md#litestar_vite.config.PathConfig) | Filesystem layout and URL prefix resolution | `root`, `resource_dir`, `bundle_dir`, `public_dir`, `ssr_output_dir`, `asset_url`, `manifest_name`, `hot_file` |
| [`RuntimeConfig`](../reference/plugin-and-config.md#litestar_vite.config.RuntimeConfig) | Dev proxy, JS executor, subprocess management, SSR transport, and asset security | `dev_mode`, `proxy_mode`, `host`, `port`, `executor`, `provisioning_mode`, `ssr_transport`, `csp_nonce`, `link_preload_headers`, `early_hints`, `immutable_cache_headers`, `trusted_proxies` |
| [`InertiaConfig`](../reference/plugin-and-config.md#litestar_vite.config.InertiaConfig) | Inertia.js protocol, shared props, SSR, and Precognition | `root_template`, `ssr`, `use_script_element`, `precognition`, `extra_static_page_props`, `shared_page_prop_types` |
| [`TypeGenConfig`](../reference/plugin-and-config.md#litestar_vite.config.TypeGenConfig) | OpenAPI, route, Inertia page-props, and AsyncAPI codegen | `output`, `openapi_path`, `routes_path`, `page_props_path`, `schemas_path`, `generate_sdk`, `generate_routes`, `generate_channels` |
| [`DeployConfig`](../reference/plugin-and-config.md#litestar_vite.config.DeployConfig) | Cloud object storage (`fsspec`) bundle upload and CDN URLs | `enabled`, `storage_backend`, `storage_options`, `asset_url`, `delete_orphaned` |

---

## Shorthand vs. Explicit Sub-Configs

`ViteConfig` accepts convenient boolean or top-level shortcuts for rapid prototyping, and normalizes them into full sub-config instances inside `__post_init__`:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from litestar_vite import PathConfig, RuntimeConfig, TypeGenConfig, ViteConfig

simple_config = ViteConfig(
    mode="spa",
    dev_mode=True,
    types=True,
)

explicit_config = ViteConfig(
    mode="spa",
    paths=PathConfig(
        root=Path("."),
        resource_dir=Path("src"),
        bundle_dir=Path("public/build"),
        asset_url="/static/",
    ),
    runtime=RuntimeConfig(
        dev_mode=True,
        executor="pnpm",
        port=5173,
    ),
    types=TypeGenConfig(
        output=Path("src/generated"),
        generate_sdk=True,
        generate_routes=True,
    ),
)
```

---

## Environment Variable Precedence

Every runtime setting can be controlled via environment variables for container and CI deployments without modifying Python code:

| Environment Variable | Maps To | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VITE_DEV_MODE` | `RuntimeConfig.dev_mode` | `"False"` (auto-enabled when running `litestar run --reload` or `--debug`) |
| `VITE_PROXY_MODE` | `RuntimeConfig.proxy_mode` | Auto-derived from `ViteConfig.mode` (`"vite"` or `"proxy"`) |
| `VITE_HOST` | `RuntimeConfig.host` | `"127.0.0.1"` |
| `VITE_PORT` | `RuntimeConfig.port` | `5173` |
| `LITESTAR_VITE_RUNTIME` / `VITE_EXECUTOR` | `RuntimeConfig.executor` | Auto-detected via `detect_runtime()` |
| `ASSET_URL` | `PathConfig.asset_url` | `"/static/"` |
| `VITE_DEPLOY_STORAGE` | `DeployConfig.storage_backend` | `None` |
| `VITE_DEPLOY_ASSET_URL` | `DeployConfig.asset_url` | `None` |
| `LITESTAR_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | `RuntimeConfig.trusted_proxies` | `None` (`"*"` or comma-separated CIDR/IP list) |

---

## JavaScript Runtime Auto-Detection & Provisioning

When `RuntimeConfig.executor` is omitted, [`detect_runtime()`](../reference/plugin-and-config.md#litestar_vite.config.detect_runtime) inspects your project root (`PathConfig.root`) and selects the matching JavaScript executor automatically:

1. `bun.lock` or `bun.lockb` → `"bun"` (`BunExecutor`)
2. `deno.lock`, `deno.json`, or `deno.jsonc` → `"deno"` (`DenoExecutor` using `deno task`, `deno install`, `deno outdated --update`)
3. `pnpm-lock.yaml` → `"pnpm"` (`PnpmExecutor`)
4. `yarn.lock` → `"yarn"` (`YarnExecutor`)
5. `package-lock.json` → `"node"` (`NodeExecutor`)
6. `package.json` `"packageManager"` field (`bun@...`, `deno@...`, `pnpm@...`, `yarn@...`, `npm@...`)
7. Fallback → `"node"`

`RuntimeConfig.provisioning_mode` controls how the runtime binary is located:

- **`"auto"` (default)**: Prefers a runtime binary installed inside the active Python virtual environment (via PEP 425 wheel extras `litestar-vite[node]`, `litestar-vite[bun]`, or `litestar-vite[deno]`) and falls back to the system `PATH`.
- **`"wheel"`**: Requires the virtual-environment binary from a runtime wheel extra and raises `ViteExecutableNotFoundError` if missing.
- **`"nodeenv"`**: Provisions a local Node environment inside the active virtual environment via `nodeenv`.
- **`"system"`**: Uses only binaries found on the host `PATH`.

---

## How the Runtime Bridge Eliminates Config Drift

Without a bridge, full-stack apps duplicate `bundle_dir`, `resource_dir`, `asset_url`, and `ssr_output_dir` across both `app.py` and `vite.config.ts`. In Litestar Vite:

1. **Python is the Single Source of Truth**: On startup (or during `litestar assets generate-types` / `litestar assets build`), Litestar writes `.litestar.json` atomically using SHA-256 `write_if_changed`.
2. **Vite Reads `.litestar.json` Automatically**: When `litestar-vite-plugin` initializes in `vite.config.ts`, it reads `.litestar.json` and configures `base`, `build.outDir`, `build.manifest`, `server.origin`, and codegen paths to match Python.
3. **Diagnostic Verification**: Run `litestar assets doctor` at any time to verify that `vite.config.ts` does not contain hardcoded overrides that conflict with `.litestar.json`. See the [Cross-Language Wire Contracts Reference](../reference/contracts.md) for the complete `.litestar.json` schema.

---

<!-- Source: docs/learn/development-and-proxy.md -->

# Development Server & Single-Port Proxy

During local development (`dev_mode=True`), Litestar Vite manages the Vite child process inside Litestar's ASGI lifespan and streams all Vite module requests and HMR WebSockets through your single Litestar port (`http://127.0.0.1:8000`).

```console
$ litestar run --reload
INFO:     Exported .litestar.json, openapi.json, and routes.json
INFO:     Starting Vite dev server (npm run dev)...
INFO:     Vite listening on http://127.0.0.1:5173 (hotfile written)
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
```

---

## Lifespan Process Supervision & Crash Recovery

When `RuntimeConfig(start_dev_server=True)` (the default when `dev_mode=True`), `VitePlugin.lifespan()` spawns and supervises the Vite dev server automatically:

1. **Startup Handshake**: Before spawning Vite, Litestar writes `.litestar.json` and exports OpenAPI/route schemas.
2. **Dynamic Port Discovery**: `litestar-vite-plugin` binds a free port and writes its bound URL (`http://127.0.0.1:5173`) to `<bundle_dir>/hot`.
3. **Capped Exponential Backoff**: If the Vite process exits unexpectedly (e.g., due to a syntax error in `vite.config.ts`), the lifespan supervisor restarts it with capped exponential backoff (`0.5s` up to `8.0s`).

### Two-Terminal Manual Workflow

If you prefer running `npm run dev` (or `litestar assets serve`) in a separate terminal tab, set `RuntimeConfig(start_dev_server=False)`. `ViteProxyMiddleware` still reads `<bundle_dir>/hot` dynamically so single-port proxying continues to work seamlessly.

---

## Proxy Modes

`RuntimeConfig.proxy_mode` (or the `VITE_PROXY_MODE` environment variable) controls which paths `ViteProxyMiddleware` forwards to the Vite dev server:

| Proxy Mode | Default For | Forwarding Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`proxy_mode="vite"`** (Allowlist) | `mode="spa"`, `mode="hybrid"`, `mode="template"` | Forwards **only** Vite internal paths (`/@vite/client`, `/@react-refresh`, `/@fs/*`, `/@id/*`, `/node_modules/*`), source entrypoints under `resource_dir`, and HMR WebSockets (`/static/vite-hmr`). Litestar handles all application routes (`/` and `/api/*`). |
| **`proxy_mode="proxy"`** (Denylist) | `mode="framework"` (`ssr`/`ssg`), `mode="external"` | Forwards every request that **does not** match a registered Litestar route or `RuntimeConfig.extra_route_prefixes` to the meta-framework dev server (Astro, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Angular CLI). |
| **`proxy_mode=None`** | Disabled | Disables `ViteProxyMiddleware` when an external reverse proxy (Caddy, Nginx, Traefik) fronts both servers. |

---

## Protecting Backend Prefix Routes

In `mode="spa"` (which registers a catch-all `/{path:path}` route for client-side routing) and `proxy_mode="proxy"`, `RuntimeConfig(extra_route_prefixes=...)` ensures backend-only prefixes never fall through to the SPA shell or meta-framework proxy when a specific URL 404s:

```python
from litestar_vite import RuntimeConfig, ViteConfig

config = ViteConfig(
    mode="spa",
    dev_mode=True,
    runtime=RuntimeConfig(
        extra_route_prefixes=("/api", "/schema", "/admin", "/health"),
    ),
)
```

With `extra_route_prefixes` configured, a request to `/api/nonexistent` returns a proper Litestar 404 Not Found JSON response instead of serving `index.html`.

---

## Same-Origin Guarantee in Development

Because the browser only ever communicates with `http://127.0.0.1:8000` (both for HTML/API requests and `/static/vite-hmr` WebSocket upgrades):

- `HttpOnly` session cookies and `SameSite=Lax` / `SameSite=Strict` CSRF cookies work without relaxed development CORS policies.
- Relative `fetch("/api/...")` and `EventSource("/api/...")` calls resolve against the exact same origin in development and production.

---

<!-- Source: docs/learn/doctor-and-troubleshooting.md -->

# Doctor CLI & Troubleshooting

Because a polyglot Python + Vite stack spans `app.py`, `.litestar.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `package.json`, and generated TypeScript artifacts, subtle mismatches in directory paths or environment variables are the most common source of setup friction.

`litestar assets doctor` inspects your live `ViteConfig` alongside your frontend workspace and runs **9 automated health checks**.

---

## Running the Doctor Command

```bash
litestar assets doctor
```

To automatically repair fixable issues (such as stale `.litestar.json` bridges or mismatched `vite.config.ts` settings) without interactive prompts:

```bash
litestar assets doctor --fix --no-prompt
```

For CI pipelines, run `--check` with `--runtime-checks` to exit with status `1` if any health check fails:

```bash
litestar assets doctor --check --runtime-checks
```

---

## Diagnostic Checks

| Check | What It Verifies | Common Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. `vite.config` Presence & Plugin** | `vite.config.ts` / `.js` exists and registers `litestar-vite-plugin` | Run `litestar assets init` or add `litestar({ input: [...] })` to `vite.config.ts` |
| **2. Path Synchronization** | `bundle_dir`, `resource_dir`, and `asset_url` in `vite.config.ts` do not conflict with `PathConfig` | Remove hardcoded `base` / `build.outDir` overrides in `vite.config.ts` so `.litestar.json` governs them |
| **3. `.litestar.json` Bridge Freshness** | `.litestar.json` exists and matches the current `ViteConfig` serialization | Run `litestar assets doctor --fix` or start the app once |
| **4. Package Dependencies** | `package.json` declares `vite >= 7.0.0` and `litestar-vite-plugin` matching the installed Python package version | Run `npm install -D litestar-vite-plugin@latest vite@^7.0.0` |
| **5. Entrypoints & Root Template** | Configured entrypoints (`src/main.tsx`, `index.html`, or `InertiaConfig.root_template`) exist on disk | Check `PathConfig.resource_dir` and `InertiaConfig.root_template` |
| **6. Production Manifest & Hotfile** | In `dev_mode=False`, verifies `<bundle_dir>/.vite/manifest.json` exists and no stale `hot` file is left behind | Run `litestar assets build` and remove stale `<bundle_dir>/hot` |
| **7. TypeGen Artifacts** | When `TypeGenConfig` is enabled, checks `openapi.json`, `routes.json`, and `schemas.ts` exist | Run `litestar assets generate-types` |
| **8. Inertia Script-Element Alignment** | When `InertiaConfig.use_script_element=True`, checks that Inertia.js client entrypoints enable `useScriptElementForInitialPage: true` | Add `defaults: { future: { useScriptElementForInitialPage: true } }` to `createInertiaApp()` |
| **9. Runtime & Environment Alignment** | Detects `RuntimeConfig.executor` / lockfile mismatches (`detect_runtime_marker`) and deprecated `VITE_PROXY_MODE=direct` overrides | Omit `RuntimeConfig.executor` to auto-detect from your lockfile and unset `VITE_PROXY_MODE=direct` |

---

## Common Symptoms & Solutions

### Missing Manifest on Startup

**Cause**: `dev_mode=False` (the default when running `litestar run` without `--reload` or `--debug`), and `litestar assets build` has not been run yet.

**Solution**:

- For local development: run `litestar run --reload` (which auto-enables `dev_mode=True`) or set `VITE_DEV_MODE=true`.
- For production: run `litestar assets build` before starting the server.

### Blank Initial Inertia Page

**Cause**: `InertiaConfig.use_script_element` defaults to `True` (emitting `<script type="application/json" data-page="app">`), while `@inertiajs/*` v2 defaults to reading the legacy `data-page` HTML attribute unless `useScriptElementForInitialPage: true` is set.

**Solution**: Pass `defaults: { future: { useScriptElementForInitialPage: true } }` to `createInertiaApp({ ... })` in both your browser entrypoint and SSR entrypoint.

### WebSocket HMR Disconnects Behind Docker or Reverse Proxy

**Cause**: Container port mappings or reverse proxies stripping WebSocket `Upgrade` headers or forwarding untrusted `X-Forwarded-Proto` headers.

**Solution**: Set `LITESTAR_TRUSTED_PROXIES="*"` (or your proxy CIDR) in your container environment and ensure your reverse proxy forwards `Upgrade` and `Connection` headers on `/vite-hmr`.

---

<!-- Source: docs/learn/index.md -->
